prog-cm2-2.body:
Introduce yourself fully: **My name is** Kossi. **I'm** eleven years old. **I live in** Atakpamé. **I'm in** CM2. **I like** football and maths.

What you can do: **I can** read. · **I can** swim. · **I can't** drive!

Your future: **Next year, I will go to** the collège!

Your favourite subject: **My favourite subject is** English!

Activity: write 6 sentences to introduce yourself to your future English teacher in 6e.
prog-cm2-2.title: I'm ready for the 6e!

prog-6e-3.body:
To talk about your family, we use **have got** (= have, own).

**I have got** (I've got) two brothers. **She has got** (she's got) a sister. Negative: **I haven't got** a dog. Question: **Have you got** a cousin? → **Yes, I have.** / **No, I haven't.**

Vocabulary: **father**, **mother**, **parents**, **brother**, **sister**, **grandfather**, **grandmother**, **uncle**, **aunt**, **cousin**, **son**, **daughter**.

The possessive **'s**: **Afi's** mother = the mother of Afi. **My father's** car = the car of my father.

Asking someone's age: **How old are you?** → **I'm twelve.** Numbers: twenty-one, thirty, forty, fifty… **one hundred**.

Practice: 1. Kofi ___ got three sisters. 2. ___ you got a brother? 3. This is the bag of Ama → This is ___ bag.
prog-6e-3.title: My family

prog-1re-7.body:
To express a **concession** (an opposition or contrast):
- **although / even though** + subject + verb: **Although** he is rich, he lives simply.
- **despite / in spite of** + noun or **-ing**: **Despite** the rain, we went out. · **In spite of being** tired, she studied.
- **however** (= but) at the start of a sentence, followed by a comma: Traditions are important. **However**, we must also be modern.
- **whereas / while** (= but on the other hand) to compare: Grandparents prefer traditional music, **whereas** young people love Afrobeat.

Vocabulary: **customs** (traditional ways of doing things) · **rites** · **heritage** (traditions and culture passed on from the past) · **festival** · **to preserve** · **globalisation** · **western influence**.
prog-1re-7.grammar: concession: although · despite · in spite of · however
prog-1re-7.title: Tradition and modernity

prog-cp1-2.body:
Count with your fingers: **one**, **two**, **three**, **four**, **five**, **six**, **seven**, **eight**, **nine**, **ten**.

**How many?** (What number?) → **Three!**

How many mangoes? → **Five mangoes.** How many pencils? → **Two pencils.**

Song: **One, two, three, four, five, once I caught a fish alive!**

Game: your teacher claps her hands, you say the number in English.
prog-cp1-2.title: Let's count!

prog-1re-6.body:
**Future continuous** (will be + -ing): an action **in progress** at a moment in the future.
This time next year, I **will be studying** at university. · In 2050, many Africans **will be working** in technology.

**Future perfect** (will have + past participle): an action **finished before** a moment in the future.
By 2030, Togo **will have built** new roads. · By the end of the year, I **will have finished** my report.

Time markers: **this time next year**, **by 2030**, **by the end of**, **in ten years' time**.

Vocabulary: **growth** (getting bigger) · **renewable energy** · **digital economy** · **infrastructure** · **young population** · **to invest**.
prog-1re-6.title: The future of Africa

prog-6e-7.body:
Sports: **football**, **basketball**, **handball**, **volleyball**, **athletics**, **swimming**, **wrestling** (like the **Evala** in Kara).

**play** + ball games: I **play** football. · **do** + other activities: I **do** athletics. · **go** + -ing: I **go** swimming.

What you can do: **I can** run fast. · **She can't** swim. · **Can you** play the drum? → **Yes, I can.**

Hobbies: **reading**, **dancing**, **singing**, **drawing**, **watching TV**.
**My hobby is** dancing. · **I like** reading.
prog-6e-7.title: Sports and hobbies

prog-cm1-3.body:
Jobs: **a teacher** (works in a school) · **a doctor** (helps sick people) · **a nurse** (helps the doctor) · **a farmer** (grows food) · **a driver** (drives a car or bus) · **a tailor** (makes clothes) · **a trader** (sells things) · **a policeman**.

**My father is a farmer.** · **My mother is a trader.**

Question: **What does your father do?** → **He is a driver.**

Your dream: **I want to be a doctor.**
prog-cm1-3.title: Jobs around me

prog-cm2-3.body:
To talk about the day before today: **yesterday**.

The verb **to be** in the past: **I was** · **you were** · **he / she / it was** · **we were** · **they were**.

**Yesterday I was at school.** · **We were happy.**

Some verbs in the past: go → **went** · play → **played** · eat → **ate** · watch → **watched**.

**Yesterday, I played football and I ate rice.**
prog-cm2-3.title: Yesterday

prog-adultes-5.body:
**Opening a meeting**: **Let's get started.** · **The purpose of this meeting is to**… · **Has everyone got the agenda?** (the list of topics for the meeting)

**Giving your opinion**: **In my view**, … · **I strongly believe**… · **I see your point, but**…
**Agreeing / disagreeing**: **I totally agree.** · **I'm afraid I disagree.** · **That's a good idea, however**…

**Negotiating**: **What's your best price?** · **Could you offer a discount?** · **If you order 100 units, we can reduce the price by 10%.** · **That sounds reasonable.** · **Let's meet halfway.** (each side gives a little)

**Closing**: **To sum up**, … · **Let's go over the action points.** · **Who is responsible for**…? · **Thank you all for coming.**
prog-adultes-5.title: Meetings and negotiation

prog-tle-4.body:
BAC II texts are often about social topics. Learn the key vocabulary.

**Democracy and human rights**: **election**, **to vote**, **citizen**, **freedom of speech**, **the rule of law**, **corruption**, **good governance**, **human rights**.

**Gender and women's empowerment**: **gender equality**, **discrimination**, **girls' education**, **early marriage**, **to empower**, **women's rights**, **breadwinner**.

**Globalisation and development**: **trade**, **developing countries**, **poverty**, **unemployment**, **brain drain** (when educated people leave their country to work abroad), **immigration**, **foreign aid**, **sustainable development**.

**Health and environment**: **HIV/AIDS**, **malaria**, **vaccination**, **climate change**, **deforestation**, **renewable energy**.

**Youth and technology**: **social media**, **cybercrime**, **digital skills**, **online learning**, **addiction**.

For each topic, prepare 3 arguments and 1 African example: you can use them again in the essay.

Practice: write 5 sentences with the vocabulary of the topic "brain drain".
prog-tle-4.title: Key BAC themes: democracy, gender, globalisation

prog-5e-6.body:
The past of **to be**: I / he / she / it **was** · you / we / they **were**.

Negative: I **wasn't** (was not) at home. · They **weren't** late.
Question: **Were** you at school yesterday? → **Yes, I was.** / **No, I wasn't.**

**There was** + singular · **There were** + plural: **There was** a big party. **There were** many people.

Time markers: **yesterday**, **last night**, **last Sunday**, **two days ago**, **in 2020**.

Example: **Last Sunday, I was in Kpalimé. There were many tourists at the waterfall.**
prog-5e-6.title: Where were you yesterday?

prog-1re-8.body:
To summarise a text is to **make it shorter** but keep **the main ideas**, in **your own words**.

Method:
1. Read the text twice and find the **main idea** of each paragraph.
2. Underline the key words, but **do not copy** the sentences.
3. Remove examples, less important numbers and repetitions.
4. Join the ideas with **linking words** (firstly, moreover, however, as a result).
5. Respect the number of words asked (for example **one third** of the text).

Useful phrases: **The text deals with**… · **According to the author**… · **The writer explains that**… · **To sum up**…

Common mistake: giving your opinion. In a summary, you stay **neutral**.
prog-1re-8.title: Summarising a text

prog-cp2-2.body:
Farm animals: **a dog** (says woof) · **a cat** (says meow) · **a goat** · **a chicken** (gives eggs) · **a cow** (gives milk) · **a pig** · **a sheep**.

What you like: **I like** cats. · **I don't like** pigs.

Animal sounds: The dog says **woof!** The cat says **meow!** The cow says **moo!**

Question: **What's this?** → **It's a goat.**
prog-cp2-2.title: Animals of the farm

prog-cm2-1.body:
Describe your town: **There is** a market. · **There is** a school. · **There are** many shops. · **There isn't** a cinema.

Places: **market** (where people buy and sell) · **hospital** · **church** · **mosque** · **school** · **river** · **football field**.

Example: **I live in** Sokodé. **There is** a big market and **there are** many schools.

Question: **Is there** a hospital in your village? → **Yes, there is.** / **No, there isn't.**
prog-cm2-1.title: My town or my village

prog-adultes-4.body:
**At the airport** (Lomé-Tokoin, Gnassingbé Eyadéma International Airport):
- **Check-in**: **Can I see your passport, please?** · **Do you have any luggage to check in?** · **Window or aisle seat?** (next to the window or next to the passage)
- **Boarding pass** (the card you need to get on the plane) · **gate** (the door to the plane) · **departure / arrival** · **delayed** (late) · **cancelled** (will not happen)

**At the hotel**:
- **I have a reservation in the name of** Amegah. · **I'd like a single / double room for two nights.** · **Is breakfast included?** · **What time is check-out?** · **The air conditioning doesn't work.**

Asking for directions: **Excuse me, how can I get to the city centre?** · **How much is a taxi to the airport?**
prog-adultes-4.title: Travel English: airport and hotel

prog-ce1-2.body:
Classroom objects: **a pen** · **a pencil** · **a ruler** (to draw straight lines) · **a book** · **a bag** · **a slate** (a small board to write on) · **a chalk** · **a table** · **a chair**.

**What's this?** → **It's a ruler.**

Classroom phrases: **Open your book.** · **Close your book.** · **Listen!** · **Be quiet, please.** · **Thank you, teacher!**
prog-ce1-2.title: My classroom

prog-1re-5.body:
**Defining relative clause**: it is **necessary** to know who or what we are talking about. No commas, **that** is possible.
The students **who passed** will go to Terminale. · The phone **that I bought** is broken.

**Non-defining relative clause**: it adds **extra information**. Between **commas**, never **that**.
Lomé, **which is the capital of Togo**, has a big harbour. · My father, **who is a doctor**, works at the CHU.

**whose** = possession: the girl **whose** mother is a teacher.
**which** can refer to a whole sentence: He passed his BAC, **which** surprised everybody.

We can leave out who / which / that when they are the object in a defining clause: The book (that) I read was great.
prog-1re-5.title: Relative clauses: defining or non-defining?

prog-4e-2.body:
**Comparative** (more… than): short adjective + **-er than**: Lomé is **bigger than** Kara. · long adjective: **more** + adjective + **than**: Lomé is **more expensive than** Atakpamé.

**Superlative** (the most…): **the** + adjective + **-est**: Mount Agou is **the highest** mountain in Togo. · **the most** + long adjective: **the most beautiful** town.

Equality: **as** + adjective + **as**: Kofi is **as tall as** his father. Less: **not as… as** / **less… than**.

Irregular: good → **better** → **the best** · bad → **worse** → **the worst** · far → **farther** → **the farthest**.

Spelling: big → bi**gger**, hot → ho**tter**, easy → eas**ier**, happy → happ**iest**.

Practice: 1. Ama is (tall) than Afi. 2. This is (good) restaurant in town. 3. English is (easy) than maths for me.
prog-4e-2.title: Comparing towns

prog-cp2-3.body:
Toys: **a ball** · **a doll** (a toy baby) · **a car** (a small toy car) · **a kite** (it flies in the wind) · **a bike** · **a skipping rope** (a rope to jump over).

**I have got** a ball. · **She has got** a doll.

Playground games: **Let's play football!** · **Let's play hide and seek!** (one child looks for the others) · **Let's jump!**

Question: **What's your favourite toy?** → **My favourite toy is my kite.**
prog-cp2-3.title: My toys and games

prog-5e-7.body:
The weather: **It's sunny.** · **It's hot.** · **It's cloudy.** · **It's windy.** · **It's raining.** · **It's stormy.** (lots of wind, rain and thunder)

In Togo, there are two main seasons: **the rainy season** (when it rains a lot) and **the dry season** (when it does not rain). From December to February, **the harmattan** blows: a dry, dusty wind from the Sahara.

Question: **What's the weather like today?** → **It's hot and humid.**

Advice: **When it rains, take an umbrella.** · **During the harmattan, drink a lot of water.**
prog-5e-7.title: Weather and seasons in Togo

prog-1re-2.body:
The passive is made with **to be** in the right tense + **past participle**.

- present: Smartphones **are used** everywhere.
- present continuous: A new road **is being built**.
- past: The telephone **was invented** by Bell.
- present perfect: Many diseases **have been eradicated**.
- future: The results **will be announced** tomorrow.
- modal: Plastic **must be recycled**.

Passive with two objects: They gave **the students** new computers. → **The students were given** new computers.

Impersonal structures: **It is said that**… · **It is believed that**… (people say that, people think that).

Vocabulary: **invention**, **to invent**, **research**, **scientist**, **device**, **artificial intelligence**, **the Internet**, **to download**, **mobile money**.

Practice: put into the passive. 1. Engineers are building a new bridge. 2. Someone has stolen my bike. 3. They will open the new hospital next year.
prog-1re-2.title: Science and technology

prog-cp2-4.body:
Clothes: **a shirt** · **a T-shirt** · **a dress** · **a skirt** · **trousers** · **shorts** · **shoes** · **a cap** (a hat for the sun).

With a colour: **a blue shirt** · **a red dress** (in English, the colour comes **before** the noun).

**I'm wearing** a uniform. (I have a uniform on my body now.)

Question: **What colour is your dress?** → **It's yellow.**
prog-cp2-4.title: My clothes

prog-3e-5.body:
To report what someone said (**reported speech**), we use **say** or **tell**.

If the reporting verb is in the **present**, the tenses do not change: She **says**, "I **am** tired." → She **says** she **is** tired.

If the verb is in the **past** (said, told), we move the tenses back:
- present → past: "I **live** in Kara." → He said he **lived** in Kara.
- will → would: "I **will** come." → She said she **would** come.
- can → could: "We **can** help." → They said they **could** help.

Pronouns: "**I** love **my** school." → Ama said **she** loved **her** school.

**tell** + person: He **told me** that he was hungry. · **say** with no person: He **said** that he was hungry.
prog-3e-5.title: Reporting what people say

prog-2nde-7.body:
Advanced comparisons:
- **the + comparative…, the + comparative**: **The more** you read, **the better** you write. · **The bigger** the city, **the higher** the prices.
- **comparative + and + comparative** (more and more): Lomé is getting **bigger and bigger**. Life is **more and more expensive**.
- **not as… as**: The village is **not as noisy as** the town.
- **much / far + comparative** (a lot more): Life in town is **much more** expensive.

Vocabulary: **crowded** (full of people) · **noisy** · **quiet** · **peaceful** · **pollution** · **traffic jam** (too many cars, nobody can move) · **facilities** (useful buildings and services) · **rural exodus** (people leaving villages to live in towns).
prog-2nde-7.title: Town life or village life?

prog-4e-5.body:
The **past continuous** describes an action **in progress** in the past.
Form: **was / were** + verb + **-ing**. At 8 o'clock, I **was eating**. They **were playing** football.

With the past simple: a long action **interrupted** by a short action.
**I was walking** home **when** it **started** to rain.
**While** she **was cooking**, the lights **went** out.

**when** + short action (past simple) · **while** + long action (past continuous).

Negative: I **wasn't** sleeping. Question: What **were you doing** at 9 p.m.?
prog-4e-5.title: What were you doing?

prog-5e-1.body:
The **present simple** is for habits, things we do often.

I / you / we / they **get up** · he / she / it **gets up** (we add **-s** for he, she, it).

Negative: I **don't** play · she **doesn't** play. Question: **Do** you play? **Does** she play?

Routine verbs: **wake up**, **get up**, **wash**, **get dressed**, **have breakfast**, **go to school**, **come back home**, **do my homework**, **go to bed**.

Adverbs of frequency go **before** the verb: **always** (100%), **usually** (most of the time), **often** (many times), **sometimes** (not often), **never** (0%). But **after** to be: She **is always** late.

Example: I **always** get up at six. My brother **never** washes the dishes.

Practice: 1. She (go) to school by bus. 2. We (not / watch) TV in the morning. 3. ___ he (like) rice?
prog-5e-1.title: My daily routine

ex-past-simple.body:
We use the **past simple** for finished actions in the past, often with yesterday, last week, in 2020, ago.

Regular verbs: add **-ed**.
work → **worked**, play → **played**, study → **studied**

Irregular verbs must be learned by heart.
go → **went**, eat → **ate**, see → **saw**, have → **had**, buy → **bought**

Negative: didn't + base verb.
I **didn't go** to school yesterday.

Question: Did + subject + base verb?
**Did** you **see** the match?
ex-past-simple.title: The past simple

ex-lesson-essay.body:
An argumentative essay follows a clear plan: **introduction**, **arguments**, **counter-argument**, **conclusion**.

**Introduction**: hook, context, then your thesis. "While some believe…, this essay will argue that…"

**Arguments**: one idea per paragraph, with an example. Start with **Firstly**, **Moreover**, **Furthermore**.

**Counter-argument**: show the other side, then answer it. **However**, **On the other hand**, **Admittedly**…

**Conclusion**: sum up and open the debate. **To conclude**, **All in all**.
ex-lesson-essay.title: Structuring an argumentative essay

prog-adultes-6.body:
**Welcoming a customer**: **Good morning, how may I help you?** · **What can I do for you today?**

**Listening to a complaint**: **I'm sorry to hear that.** · **Could you tell me exactly what happened?** · **I completely understand your frustration.**

**Apologising**: **I do apologise for the inconvenience.** · **We're very sorry about the delay.**

**Offering a solution**: **I can offer you a refund** (your money back) **or a replacement.** · **We'll deliver it tomorrow at no extra cost.** · **Let me check that for you.**

**Making a complaint (customer)**: **I'd like to make a complaint.** · **The product I bought is faulty** (it does not work properly). · **I'd like a refund, please.**

**Ending**: **Is there anything else I can help you with?** · **Thank you for your patience.**
prog-adultes-6.title: Customer service and complaints

prog-3e-6.body:
**Relative pronouns** help us avoid repeating a noun.

- **who** for a person: Emmanuel Adebayor is a footballer **who** played for Arsenal.
- **which** for a thing: Kara is a city **which** is famous for the Evala.
- **where** for a place: Kpalimé is a town **where** you can see beautiful waterfalls.
- **that** can replace who or which: The fish **that** we ate was delicious.

Examples: The woman **who** sells cloth is my aunt. · The book **which** I bought is interesting.

Method: join two sentences. Ama is a nurse. **She** works in Sokodé. → Ama is a nurse **who** works in Sokodé.
prog-3e-6.title: People and places of Togo

prog-4e-3.body:
**be going to**: a plan already decided, an intention. I **am going to** visit my uncle next weekend. Look at the clouds! It **is going to** rain.

**will**: a decision made at the moment of speaking, a promise, a prediction. I'm thirsty. → I **will** (I'll) buy some water. I **will** help you. In 2050, people **will** travel to Mars.

Negative: **won't** (= will not): I **won't** be late. · I'm **not going to** watch TV.

Time markers: **tomorrow**, **next week**, **next year**, **soon**, **in the future**, **one day**.

Example: After the BEPC, I **am going to** study in a lycée in Lomé. One day, I **will** be a doctor.

Practice: will or going to? 1. The phone is ringing. I ___ answer it. 2. We ___ visit Kpalimé next Sunday (it is already planned). 3. I think it ___ be hot tomorrow.
prog-4e-3.title: Plans and predictions

prog-ce2-3.body:
Rooms: **the bedroom** (where you sleep) · **the kitchen** (where you cook) · **the living room** (where you sit with your family) · **the bathroom** (where you wash) · **the yard** (outside, around the house).

**Where is Mum?** → **She is in the kitchen.** · **Where is the cat?** → **It's in the yard.**

Objects: **a bed** · **a table** · **a chair** · **a door** · **a window**.

Sentence: **My house has got three rooms.**
prog-ce2-3.title: My house

prog-6e-1.body:
To greet people and introduce yourself, we use the verb **to be**.

**I am** (I'm) · **you are** (you're) · **he / she / it is** (he's, she's) · **we are** · **they are**

Greetings: **Good morning!** (in the morning) · **Good afternoon!** (in the afternoon) · **Good evening!** (in the evening) · **Hello!** / **Hi!** (with friends). When you leave: **Goodbye!** / **See you tomorrow!**

Introducing yourself: **My name is** Ama. **I'm** eleven. **I'm from** Togo. **How are you?** → **I'm fine, thank you. And you?**

Possessive adjectives: **my** (belongs to me), **your** (belongs to you), **his** (belongs to a boy or man), **her** (belongs to a girl or woman), **our**, **their**. Example: **Her** name is Afi. **His** name is Kofi.

Practice: complete with am, is or are. 1. I ___ a pupil. 2. Kofi ___ my friend. 3. We ___ in 6e.
prog-6e-1.title: Greetings and introductions

prog-2nde-2.body:
**Relative pronouns** join two sentences.

- **who**: for a person. Sylvanus Olympio is the man **who** led Togo to independence.
- **which**: for a thing or an animal. The Lomé harbour is a port **which** serves many countries.
- **that**: person or thing (everyday language): The book **that** I'm reading is interesting.
- **whose**: possession. Nelson Mandela is a leader **whose** courage inspired the world.
- **where**: a place. Kara is the town **where** I was born.

We can leave out who / which / that when they are the object: The film (**that**) we watched was great.

Vocabulary: **leader**, **independence**, **freedom**, **to fight for**, **hero**, **to inspire**, **achievement**.

Practice: 1. The girl ___ won the prize is my sister. 2. This is the man ___ car was stolen. 3. The village ___ my grandmother lives is far.
prog-2nde-2.grammar: relative pronouns: who, which, that, whose, where
prog-2nde-2.title: People who changed Africa

prog-3e-4.body:
In Togo, the BEPC English exam lasts **2 hours** and has a **coefficient of 2**. It has three parts.

**1. Reading comprehension**: a text, often about life in Togo or in Africa (health, traditions, school, environment). **True or False** questions (copy the sentence from the text that proves your answer), multiple-choice questions and short answers. Always answer with **full sentences**: Where does the boy live? → **He lives in Kara.**

**2. Grammar and language use**: change a sentence into the **question form**, the **passive**, **reported speech**, put verbs in the right tense, find the opposite of a word (**un**able, **im**possible).

**3. Writing**: a **dialogue** or a **letter**. For a dialogue, write the name of each person followed by a colon (**Ali:** … **Kofi:** …), 8 to 12 lines, with natural phrases (**Hey! How are you?** · **I don't agree with you.** · **You should…**). For a friendly letter: town and date at the top right, **Dear Kofi,** then the introduction, the body, the conclusion and **Your friend,** + your first name.

Tips: read the questions first, manage your time (about 40 minutes per part), and keep 10 minutes to check your work (**-s** for he/she/it, irregular verbs).

Practice: write a dialogue of 8 lines between two friends talking about their plans after the BEPC.
prog-3e-4.title: BEPC method: reading and writing

prog-6e-5.body:
Clothes: **shirt**, **T-shirt**, **trousers**, **shorts**, **dress**, **skirt**, **shoes**, **sandals**, **socks**, **cap**, **uniform**, **pagne** (a pagne is also called a **wrapper**).

In English, the **adjective** goes **before** the noun and never takes -s: **a blue shirt**, **two red dresses**.

To say what you have on now: **I'm wearing** a khaki uniform. · **She's wearing** a yellow dress.

Questions: **What colour is your cap?** → **It's black.** · **What are you wearing today?**

At the market: **How much is this dress?** → **It's three thousand CFA francs.**
prog-6e-5.title: Clothes and colours

prog-tle-7.body:
**Mixed conditional**: a past condition with a present result (or the opposite).
**If** I **had studied** medicine, I **would be** a doctor now. (past → present)
**If** she **were** more careful, she **wouldn't have lost** her phone. (present → past)

Other condition words:
- **unless** = if… not: You won't pass **unless** you work hard.
- **provided (that) / as long as** = only if: I'll lend you my book **provided that** you return it.
- **in case** = because something might happen: Take an umbrella **in case** it rains.
- **otherwise** = if not: Hurry up, **otherwise** you'll miss the bus.

Remember: never use **will** just after **if**, **unless**, **provided that**, **in case**.
prog-tle-7.title: Conditions: mixed conditionals and connectors

prog-adultes-2.body:
On the phone, stay **polite** and **clear**.

**Answering**: **Good morning, Togo Services, Afi speaking. How can I help you?**
**Calling**: **Hello, this is** Kofi Mensah **from** ABC Company. **Could I speak to** Mr Ayivi, **please?**

**Asking someone to wait**: **Hold on, please.** · **One moment, please.** · **I'll put you through.**
**Leaving a message**: **He's not available at the moment. Can I take a message?** · **Could you ask him to call me back?**

**Polite requests**: **Could you** send me the invoice? · **Would you mind** spell**ing** your name? · **I'd like to** book a meeting.

Spelling: learn the alphabet in English (A [eɪ], E [iː], I [aɪ], G [dʒiː], J [dʒeɪ], R [ɑː]…).

**Ending**: **Thank you for calling.** · **Have a nice day.** · **Goodbye.**

Practice: write a 6-line dialogue to make an appointment with a supplier.
prog-adultes-2.title: Phone calls and polite requests

prog-3e-1.body:
The **present perfect** links the past to the present: an experience, or an action that continues until now.

Form: **have / has** + past participle: I **have visited** Ghana. She **has lost** her key. Irregular: go → **gone**, see → **seen**, eat → **eaten**, write → **written**, be → **been**.

Experience: **Have you ever** taken a plane? → **Yes, I have.** / **No, I have never** taken a plane.

Duration: **since** + starting point (**since** 2020, **since** Monday) · **for** + length of time (**for** three years, **for** two hours). I **have lived** in Lomé **for** ten years.

Other words: **already** (before now), **yet** (in questions and negatives), **just** (a very short time ago): I have **just** finished.

Present perfect or past simple? I **have been** to Kara (experience, no date). I **went** to Kara **last year** (exact time → past simple).

Practice: 1. She has lived here ___ 2019. 2. I have known him ___ five years. 3. ___ you ever (eat) fufu?
prog-3e-1.grammar: present perfect · since / for · ever / never
prog-3e-1.title: Life experiences

ex-lesson-email.body:
A professional email has **five parts**: subject, greeting, purpose, details and closing.

**Greeting**: Dear Mr Mensah, / Dear Sir or Madam, / Hello Ama, (less formal)

**Purpose** (first line): I am writing to **confirm** our meeting. / I am writing **regarding** your order.

**Useful phrases**: Please **find attached** the report. Could you **let me know** by Friday? I **look forward to hearing** from you.

**Closing**: Best regards, / Kind regards, / Yours faithfully, (when you don't know the name)
ex-lesson-email.title: Writing a professional email

prog-cp2-1.body:
Introduce your family: **This is my mother.** · **This is my father.** · **This is my brother.** · **This is my sister.** · **This is my baby.**

**I love my family!**

Grandparents: **grandma** (your mother's or father's mother) · **grandpa** (your mother's or father's father).

Question: **Who is this?** (asking about a person) → **It's my grandma.**

Activity: draw your family and write under each person: mother, father, brother, sister.
prog-cp2-1.title: My family

ex-present-simple.body:
We use the **present simple** for habits, routines and things that are always true.

With I, you, we, they: the verb does not change.
I **play** football. They **live** in Lomé.

With he, she, it: add **-s** (or **-es**).
She **plays** football. He **watches** TV. It **goes** fast.

Negative: don't / doesn't + verb.
I **don't like** coffee. She **doesn't work** on Sunday.

Question: Do / Does + subject + verb?
**Do** you speak English? **Does** he live here?
ex-present-simple.title: The present simple

prog-3e-8.body:
After some verbs, we use the verb + **-ing**; after others, **to** + verb.

**-ing** after: **like**, **love**, **enjoy**, **hate**, **finish**, **stop**, **be good at**: I **enjoy dancing**. She is **good at drawing**.

**to** + verb after: **want**, **decide**, **hope**, **need**, **learn**, **would like**: I **want to be** a pilot. We **hope to pass** the BEPC.

After a preposition (at, in, for, of), always **-ing**: Thanks **for helping** me. · I'm interested **in learning** Chinese.

Plans after the BEPC: **I'd like to go** to the lycée. · **I'm thinking of studying** science.
prog-3e-8.title: Likes, dislikes and plans

ex-lesson-family.body:
Use **have got** or **have** to talk about your family.

I **have** two brothers and one sister. She **has** a cat.

Family words: **mother**, **father**, **brother**, **sister**, **grandmother**, **uncle**, **aunt**, **cousin**.

Possessive 's: This is **Afi's** bag. My **father's** name is Koffi.
ex-lesson-family.title: Talking about my family

prog-cm1-1.body:
My day: I **wake up** at 6. · I **wash** my face. · I **eat** breakfast. · I **go to school**. · I **play** with my friends. · I **do** my homework. · I **go to bed**.

With he / she, we add **-s**: She **goes** to school. He **plays** football.

The time: **What time is it?** → **It's seven o'clock.**

Activity: tell about your day in 5 sentences in English.
prog-cm1-1.title: My day

prog-universite-6.body:
Reading **critically** means judging how **strong** an argument is.

Questions to ask yourself:
- **What is the claim?** (What is the main idea the author wants to prove?)
- **What evidence supports it?** (Data, studies, examples?)
- **Is the source reliable?** (Author, date, institution)
- **Are there assumptions?** (Ideas taken as true without proof)
- **What are the counter-arguments?**

Common reasoning mistakes (**fallacies**):
- **Generalisation**: "All young people are lazy."
- **False cause**: A happens before B, so A causes B.
- **Appeal to authority**: "It's true because a famous person said it."
- **Either/or** (false choice between only two options): "Either we build factories or we stay poor."

Expressions: **The author claims that**… · **This argument is weakened by**… · **The evidence suggests**… · **However, it fails to consider**…
prog-universite-6.title: Critical reading: analysing an argument

prog-universite-5.body:
A professional email must be **clear**, **short** and **polite**.

A precise **subject line**: "Request for an appointment – Thesis supervision".

**Greeting**: **Dear Professor Adjovi,** · **Dear Dr Mensah,** · **Dear Sir or Madam,**

**Opening**: **I hope this email finds you well.** · **I am writing regarding**…

**Polite request**: **Could you please**…? · **I would be grateful if you could**… · **Would it be possible to**…?

**Attachment**: **Please find attached**…

**Closing**: **Thank you in advance for your help.** · **Kind regards,** / **Best regards,** + full name, course of study and student number.

Avoid: text-message abbreviations (pls, thx), capital letters everywhere (= shouting), an email with no subject.
prog-universite-5.title: Writing professional emails

prog-4e-7.body:
**Adverbs of manner** tell us **how** we do something.
We often make them with **adjective + -ly**: quick → **quickly**, slow → **slowly**, careful → **carefully**, easy → **easily**, happy → **happily**.

Irregular: good → **well** · fast → **fast** · hard → **hard** (work hard) · late → **late**.

Position: usually **after the verb** or after the object. She runs **fast**. He plays football **well**. Drive **carefully**!

Adjective or adverb? Kofi is a **good** player (adjective + noun). Kofi plays **well** (verb + adverb).
prog-4e-7.title: How do you play?

prog-3e-7.body:
To give advice:
- **should / shouldn't** + verb: You **should** talk to your parents. · You **shouldn't** stay up late.
- **had better** (+ verb): strong advice, with a consequence: You**'d better** study, or you'll fail.
- **If I were you, I would**…: **If I were you, I would** say no.
- **Why don't you**…?: **Why don't you** join a club?

Problems of young people: **peer pressure** (when friends push you to do something) · **drugs** · **early pregnancy** (having a baby too young) · **school dropout** (leaving school too early) · **addiction to phones**.

Example dialogue: "My friends want me to smoke." → "**You shouldn't** listen to them. **If I were you, I would** stay away from them."
prog-3e-7.grammar: advice: should · had better · if I were you
prog-3e-7.title: Giving advice to young people

prog-2nde-6.body:
To make a **deduction** about the present:
- **must** = it is almost certainly true: The lights are on. They **must be** at home.
- **might / may / could** = it is possible: She isn't here. She **might be** ill.
- **can't** = it is impossible: He **can't be** hungry, he has just eaten.

About the past: modal + **have** + past participle.
The road is wet. It **must have rained**. · He **can't have stolen** it, he was with me. · She **might have missed** the bus.

Be careful: **mustn't** means something is not allowed, not a deduction. The opposite of "must be" (certainty) is **can't be**.
prog-2nde-6.grammar: modals of deduction: must · might · can't
prog-2nde-6.title: Deduction: must, might, can't

prog-6e-2.body:
To show an object near you: **this** · an object far from you: **that**. In the plural: **these** / **those**.

**This is** a **pen**. **That is** a **blackboard**. **These are** my **books**.

Article: **a** before a consonant sound (**a** ruler, **a** bag), **an** before a vowel sound (**an** eraser, **an** exercise book).

Plural: we add **-s** (a book → two book**s**), **-es** after s, x, ch, sh (a box → box**es**). Irregular plurals: man → **men**, woman → **women**, child → **children**.

Useful questions: **What is this?** → It's a pencil. **Where is my bag?** → It's **on** the table / **under** the desk / **in** the cupboard.

Practice: a or an? 1. ___ apple 2. ___ chair 3. ___ orange.
prog-6e-2.title: In the classroom

prog-universite-2.body:
**Summarise**: keep the main ideas of a text in far fewer words. **Paraphrase**: say an idea again in **your own words**, without changing the meaning.

Paraphrasing method:
1. Read and understand the sentence.
2. Hide it and write the idea with different words and a different structure.
3. Compare with the original and **cite the source**.

Techniques: synonyms (**increase** → **rise**), change the word type (**to develop** → **development**), active ↔ passive, change the order of the ideas.

Example: Original: "Mobile money has transformed financial access in West Africa." → Paraphrase: **Access to financial services in West Africa has changed considerably thanks to mobile payment systems** (Koné, 2022).

Copying without citing is **plagiarism** (using someone else's work as your own), and it is severely punished at university.

Practice: paraphrase: "Many young graduates leave Africa to find better opportunities abroad."
prog-universite-2.title: Summarising and paraphrasing

prog-universite-1.body:
Academic English is **formal**, **precise** and **nuanced**.

Avoid contractions: **do not** (not don't), **it is** (not it's). Avoid informal language: **a lot of** → **a considerable number of** · **get** → **obtain**, **become** · **big** → **significant**.

**Hedging** (being careful, not too sure): in research, we avoid statements that are too absolute. **This suggests that**… · **It appears that**… · **may**, **might**, **could** · **tends to** · **to some extent**.

Impersonal structures: **It can be argued that**… · **It is widely accepted that**… · **The data indicate that**…

Citing a source: **According to** Diallo (2021), … · **As Smith (2019) points out**, …

Practice: rewrite in academic style: "Lots of students don't get good jobs after university."
prog-universite-1.title: Academic writing style

prog-2nde-4.body:
**Reported speech** tells what someone said. With a reporting verb in the past (**said**, **told**), we move the tenses one step back.

- present → past: "I **am** tired." → She said (that) she **was** tired.
- present continuous → past continuous: "I **am working**." → He said he **was working**.
- past / present perfect → past perfect: "I **saw** him." → She said she **had seen** him.
- will → would: "I **will** come." → He said he **would** come.
- can → could: "I **can** swim." → She said she **could** swim.

Changes of time and place words: **today** → **that day** · **tomorrow** → **the next day** · **yesterday** → **the day before** · **here** → **there** · **this** → **that**.

**say** / **tell**: He **said** that… · He **told me** that… (tell is followed by a person).

Vocabulary: **newspaper**, **headline**, **journalist**, **to broadcast**, **social media**, **fake news**.

Practice: 1. "I live in Sokodé." → He said… 2. "We will travel tomorrow." → They said…
prog-2nde-4.title: Reporting what people say

prog-cm1-2.body:
The weather: **It's sunny** (the sun is shining) · **It's hot** · **It's raining** (water falls from the sky) · **It's windy** (there is a lot of wind) · **It's cloudy** (there are clouds).

In Togo, there is **the rainy season** (the months with a lot of rain) and **the dry season** (the months with no rain). In December and January comes **the harmattan**: it is dry and dusty.

**What's the weather like today?** → **It's hot and sunny.**

Activity: every morning, say the weather of the day in English.
prog-cm1-2.title: Weather in Togo

prog-3e-2.body:
We use the **passive** when the action is more important than the person who does it.

Form: **to be** + past participle. Present: Cocoa **is grown** in the Plateaux region. Past: This school **was built** in 1990.

Active → passive: Farmers **grow** coffee. → Coffee **is grown** (by farmers). The workers **built** the bridge. → The bridge **was built** by the workers.

Keep the tense of the original verb on **to be**: grow (present) → **is / are grown** · built (past) → **was / were built**.

Vocabulary: **cotton**, **cocoa**, **coffee**, **phosphate**, **factory**, **to produce**, **to export**, **goods**, **farmer**, **harbour** (the port of Lomé).

Practice: put these sentences in the passive. 1. People speak Ewe in the south. 2. The teacher corrected the exercises. 3. Togo exports phosphate.
prog-3e-2.title: Products and industries

prog-5e-5.body:
Big numbers: **one hundred** (100) · **two hundred and fifty** (250) · **one thousand** (1,000) · **five thousand** (5,000) · **ten thousand** (10,000).

In British English we say **and** after hundred: three hundred **and** twenty.

Asking the price: **How much is** this bag? → **It's two thousand five hundred CFA francs.** · **How much are** these shoes?

Bargaining: **It's too expensive!** · **Can you reduce the price, please?** · **I'll give you two thousand.** · **OK, deal!**

Paying: **Can I pay with mobile money?** · **Here is your change.** (the money you get back)
prog-5e-5.title: Shopping and prices

prog-ce2-1.body:
Food: **rice** · **beans** · **bread** · **fish** · **meat** · **eggs** · **banana** · **mango** · **orange** · **pineapple** (a big yellow fruit with a hard skin).

Saying what you like: **I like rice.** · **I don't like fish.** · **My favourite food is fufu!**

Question: **Do you like bananas?** → **Yes, I do.** / **No, I don't.**

Drinking: **I'm thirsty. I want water, please.**
prog-ce2-1.grammar: food · I like / I don't like
prog-ce2-1.title: Food I like

prog-4e-8.body:
A friendly email has a simple structure.

**Subject**: short and clear, for example **News from Kara!**

**Greeting**: **Hi Ama,** · **Dear Kofi,**

**Introduction**: **How are you? I hope you and your family are fine.** · **Thanks for your last email.**

**Body**: give your news and ask questions. **Guess what? I passed my exams!** · **Last weekend, I went to the beach.** · **What about you?**

**Conclusion**: **Write back soon!** · **I'm looking forward to hearing from you.** · **Say hello to your parents.**

**Closing**: **Love,** / **Best wishes,** / **See you soon,** + your first name.

Tip: write short sentences and use the right tense (past simple to tell a story).
prog-4e-8.title: Writing an email to a friend

prog-tle-5.body:
To give more **force** to a sentence (formal style, very good in the BAC essay):

**Inversion** after a negative expression at the start of the sentence (auxiliary + subject):
**Never have I seen** such a beautiful place. · **Not only does** education reduce poverty, **but it also** improves health. · **Rarely do** young people read newspapers. · **No sooner had** he arrived **than** it started to rain.

**Cleft sentence**: **It is** education **that** will change Africa. · **What** we need **is** more teachers.

Emphatic **do / does / did**: I **do** understand your point.

Be careful: inversion follows the question form: Never **have I** (not "Never I have").
prog-tle-5.title: Emphasis and inversion

prog-universite-3.body:
A good presentation is **introduced**, **structured** and **guided** by transition expressions (**signposting**).

**Opening**: **Good morning, everyone. Today I'm going to talk about**… · **My presentation is divided into three parts.**

**Moving from one part to the next**: **Let's move on to**… · **Now I'd like to turn to**… · **As you can see on this slide**…

**Stressing a point**: **The key point here is**… · **It's important to note that**…

**Concluding**: **To sum up**, … · **In conclusion**, … · **Thank you for your attention. Are there any questions?**

**Answering questions**: **That's a good question.** · **Could you repeat the question, please?** · **I'm not sure, but I think**…

Tips: speak slowly, look at your audience, one idea per slide, practise out loud.

Practice: prepare the introduction (1 minute) of a presentation about your field of study.
prog-universite-3.title: Giving an oral presentation

prog-6e-4.body:
The days: **Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday** (always with a capital letter).

The months: **January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, December**.

The date: **What's the date today?** → **It's Monday, the fifth of October.** We use ordinal numbers: first, second, third, fourth, fifth… twentieth.

The time: **What time is it?** → **It's eight o'clock** (8:00). **It's half past eight** (8:30). **It's a quarter past nine** (9:15). **It's a quarter to ten** (9:45). **It's ten past seven** (7:10).

Prepositions: **on** Monday · **in** January · **at** seven o'clock.

Practice: write in words. 1. 6:30 2. 1st January 3. The time is 10:15.
prog-6e-4.grammar: telling the time · days and months
prog-6e-4.title: Days, dates and time

prog-4e-6.body:
With a **countable** noun (eggs, oranges): **many**, **a few** (a small number), **few** (not many).
With an **uncountable** noun (sugar, water, rice): **much**, **a little** (a small amount), **little** (not much).
**a lot of / lots of** works with both, mostly in positive sentences.

Examples: There are **a lot of** mangoes. · I don't eat **much** sugar. · How **many** bananas? · Add **a little** salt. · I have **a few** friends in Lomé.

Too / enough: **too much** sugar · **too many** sweets · **enough** water (the right amount of water).

Health: Eat **a lot of** fruit and vegetables, but not **too much** salt or **too many** fried foods.
prog-4e-6.grammar: much / many / a lot of / a few / a little
prog-4e-6.title: Quantities: much, many, a few, a little

prog-tle-2.body:
Prepare the BAC II **essay** with a simple, clear plan.

**Introduction** (3 or 4 sentences): present the topic, rephrase the question, announce your plan. **Nowadays**, … **This essay will first examine**…, **then**…

**Body** (2 or 3 paragraphs): **one idea per paragraph**, a topic sentence, an explanation, **a concrete example** (Togo, Africa, the world).

**Conclusion**: sum up your position and open the debate. **To conclude**, … **It would be interesting to**…

Useful expressions: **It is widely believed that**… · **There is no doubt that**… · **One may argue that**… · **This shows that**… · **As far as I am concerned**, …

Traps to avoid: translating word for word from your first language · sentences that are too long · forgetting the **-s** of the 3rd person · not respecting the number of words asked.

Practice: write the plan (introduction + 2 ideas + conclusion) for the topic: "Is it better to study in Togo or abroad?"
prog-tle-2.title: BAC II method: writing an essay

prog-tle-6.body:
**Phrasal verbs** (verb + particle) are very common in BAC texts.

- **look after** = take care of · **look for** = try to find · **look forward to** = be excited about something in the future
- **give up** = stop trying · **carry on** = continue · **set up** = create, start (a business)
- **bring up** = raise (a child) · **grow up** = become an adult · **turn down** = refuse
- **find out** = discover · **put off** = delay, do later · **run out of** = have no more of
- **get on with** = have a good relationship with · **take after** = look or act like (a parent)
- **deal with** = handle, take care of · **cope with** = manage a difficult situation

Examples: She **set up** her own business in Lomé. · Don't **give up** your studies! · We have **run out of** water.
prog-tle-6.title: Essential phrasal verbs

prog-ce2-4.body:
The 12 months: **January**, **February**, **March**, **April**, **May**, **June**, **July**, **August**, **September**, **October**, **November**, **December**.

Birthdays: **When is your birthday?** → **My birthday is in March.**

In Togo, school starts again **in September**. The long holidays start **in July**.

Song: **Happy birthday to you!**
prog-ce2-4.title: Months and birthdays

prog-5e-2.body:
**Countable** nouns can be counted: a banana, two **bananas**, three **eggs**. **Uncountable** nouns cannot be counted: **rice**, **water**, **bread**, **oil**, **sugar**, **money**.

**some** in positive sentences: I want **some** tomatoes. There is **some** water.
**any** in negative sentences and questions: There isn't **any** milk. Have you got **any** onions?

Quantity: **How many** + countable: **How many** mangoes do you want? · **How much** + uncountable: **How much** rice do you need?

Prices (in CFA francs): **How much is it?** → **It's five hundred CFA francs.** **How much are the oranges?**

At the market: **Can I have** two kilos of tomatoes, please? · **Here you are.** · **That's too expensive!** · **Can you reduce the price?**

Practice: some or any? 1. I've got ___ bread. 2. Is there ___ juice? 3. How ___ (much / many) eggs?
prog-5e-2.grammar: countable / uncountable · some / any · how much / how many
prog-5e-2.title: At the market

prog-tle-1.body:
Reading comprehension gives a lot of points in the BAC II. Always follow the same method.

**1. Before reading**: read the title, the source and the questions. They tell you the topic of the text.

**2. First reading**: read the whole text without stopping at new words. Who? What? Where? When? Why?

**3. True or False**: write **True** or **False**, then **copy the exact sentence** from the text that proves it, in quotation marks, with the line number if possible.

**4. Open questions**: answer in **your own words** with complete sentences. Do not copy whole paragraphs.

**5. Vocabulary**: for a **synonym** or an **antonym**, keep the same type of word (a verb for a verb) and the same tense.

**6. Read again**: check agreement (he **has**, she **doesn't**), irregular verbs and punctuation.

Time management: share your time between the three parts (comprehension, language, essay) and keep 15 minutes to read your work again.

Practice: take a paper from the Exams section and apply the method step by step.
prog-tle-1.title: BAC II method: reading comprehension

prog-6e-8.body:
Farm animals: **dog**, **cat**, **goat**, **sheep**, **cow**, **chicken**, **pig**, **duck**.
Wild animals: **lion**, **elephant**, **monkey**, **snake**, **crocodile**, **antelope**. **Fazao-Malfakassa** National Park is home to elephants.

Describing an animal: The elephant **is big** and **grey**. It **has got** a long trunk (its long nose). · The monkey **is** clever.

Some irregular plurals: sheep → **sheep** · mouse → **mice** · fish → **fish**.

Questions: **Is there** a cat in your house? → **Yes, there is.** · **How many** goats **has** your grandfather **got**?
prog-6e-8.title: Animals around us

prog-1re-4.body:
In the BAC I, the writing task often asks you to **give your opinion** in an organised way.

Structure of a paragraph: **topic sentence** (your main idea) → **2 or 3 arguments** with examples → **concluding sentence**.

Linking words:
- adding: **firstly**, **secondly**, **moreover**, **furthermore**, **in addition**
- contrast: **however**, **but**, **although**, **on the other hand**, **whereas**
- cause: **because**, **since**, **as**, **due to**
- result: **so**, **therefore**, **as a result**, **consequently**
- example: **for example**, **for instance**, **such as**
- concluding: **to conclude**, **in conclusion**, **all in all**

Giving your opinion: **In my opinion**, … · **I strongly believe that** … · **From my point of view**, …

Example: **In my opinion**, school uniforms are useful. **Firstly**, they reduce differences between rich and poor pupils. **Moreover**, they save time in the morning. **However**, some students feel they cannot express their personality. **All in all**, I think the advantages are more important.

Practice: write an 80-word paragraph: "Should mobile phones be allowed at school?"
prog-1re-4.title: Writing an argumentative paragraph

prog-tle-8.body:
Vocabulary for the other big BAC II themes:

**Health**: **public health**, **HIV/AIDS**, **malaria**, **vaccination campaign**, **traditional medicine**, **healthcare system**, **to prevent**, **epidemic**.

**Environment**: **climate change**, **global warming**, **deforestation**, **desertification**, **coastal erosion** (the sea taking the land, in Lomé and Aného), **waste management**, **renewable energy**, **to recycle**.

**Youth and technology**: **social media**, **cyberbullying** (hurting people online), **digital divide** (the gap between people with and without internet), **online learning**, **unemployment**, **entrepreneurship**, **start-up**.

**Education**: **literacy** (being able to read and write), **school enrolment**, **girls' education**, **dropout rate**, **vocational training** (learning a job or a trade).

For each theme, prepare: 3 causes, 3 consequences, 3 solutions, 1 example from Togo.
prog-tle-8.title: Key BAC themes: health, environment, youth

prog-6e-6.body:
Meals: **breakfast** (the morning meal) · **lunch** (the midday meal) · **dinner** (the evening meal).

Dishes and drinks: **rice**, **beans**, **fufu**, **akumé**, **fish**, **chicken**, **soup**, **bread**, **tea**, **juice**, **water**.

Saying what you like: **I like** fufu. · **I love** pineapple juice. · **I don't like** fish. · **I hate** onions.
With he / she: She **likes** rice. He **doesn't like** tea.

**a / an** for one thing you can count (an egg) · **some** for a quantity (some rice, some water).

Question: **What do you have for breakfast?** → **I have bread and tea.**
prog-6e-6.title: Food and drinks

prog-ce1-3.body:
Keep counting: **eleven** (11) · **twelve** (12) · **thirteen** (13) · **fourteen** (14) · **fifteen** (15) · **sixteen** (16) · **seventeen** (17) · **eighteen** (18) · **nineteen** (19) · **twenty** (20).

Tip: from 13 to 19, the numbers end in **-teen**.

Age: **How old are you?** → **I'm eight.** · **My brother is eleven.**

Maths: **ten + five = fifteen** (ten plus five equals fifteen).
prog-ce1-3.title: Numbers 11 to 20

prog-1re-3.body:
**Reported questions**: no more inversion and no question mark.
- Yes / no questions → **if** / **whether**: "**Are** you ready?" → She asked me **if I was** ready.
- Questions with a question word → keep the word: "Where **do you live**?" → He asked me **where I lived**.

**Orders and requests** → **to** + verb (or **not to**):
- "**Close** the door." → He **told me to close** the door.
- "**Don't** be late." → The teacher **told us not to be** late.
- "Could you help me, please?" → She **asked me to help** her.

Do not forget to move the tenses back (see the 2nde lesson) and to change time words (**tomorrow** → **the next day**).

Useful reporting verbs: **ask**, **tell**, **order**, **advise**, **beg**, **remind**, **warn**.

Practice: 1. "Did you finish your homework?" the teacher asked me. 2. "Don't touch the cables!" he told the children. 3. "Why are you crying?" she asked him.
prog-1re-3.title: Reporting questions and orders

prog-5e-3.body:
To ask the way: **Excuse me, where is the hospital, please?** · **How can I get to the post office?** · **Is there a pharmacy near here?**

To answer, we use the **imperative** (verb with no subject): **Go straight on.** · **Turn left.** · **Turn right.** · **Take the second street on the left.** · **Cross the road.** Negative: **Don't turn** here.

Prepositions of place: **next to** (at the side of) · **opposite** (facing, on the other side) · **between** (in the middle of two things) · **behind** (at the back of) · **in front of** (before, facing the front) · **at the corner of**.

Places in town: **market**, **bank**, **church**, **mosque**, **hospital**, **police station**, **bus station**, **stadium**, **school**.

Example: The bank is **between** the market and the church, **opposite** the stadium.

Practice: write the directions. 1. Tell someone to go to the right. 2. Say where the pharmacy is: the school is just at its side. 3. Tell someone not to turn.
prog-5e-3.title: Asking for directions

prog-ce1-1.body:
Parts of the body: **head** · **eyes** · **ears** · **nose** · **mouth** · **hands** · **legs** · **feet**.

Play "Simon says" in English: **Touch your head!** · **Clap your hands!** · **Stand up!** · **Sit down!** · **Jump!**

Song: **Head, shoulders, knees and toes, knees and toes!**

Hygiene: **Wash your hands** before eating!
prog-ce1-1.title: My body

prog-cp1-4.body:
Fruits from Togo: **a mango** · **a banana** · **an orange** · **a pineapple** · **a papaya** · **a coconut** · **an avocado**.

What I like: **I like mangoes.** · **I don't like papaya.**

Colours of fruits: The banana is **yellow**. The orange is **orange**. The avocado is **green**.

Question: **Do you like pineapples?** → **Yes, I do!** / **No, I don't.**
prog-cp1-4.title: My favourite fruits

prog-ce1-4.body:
Actions: **run** · **jump** · **swim** · **dance** · **sing** · **climb** · **read** · **write**.

Saying what you can do: **I can swim.** · **I can't fly!**

Question: **Can you dance?** → **Yes, I can.** / **No, I can't.**

Game "Simon says": **Simon says jump!** · **Simon says sing!**
prog-ce1-4.title: I can run!

prog-2nde-1.body:
Tenses review: present simple (**I study** every day) · present continuous (**I am studying** now) · past simple (**I studied** yesterday) · present perfect (**I have studied** English for five years) · future (**I will study** abroad).

**Question tags** (short questions at the end, like "right?") repeat the auxiliary, in the opposite form:
- Positive sentence → negative tag: You **are** tired, **aren't you?** · She **likes** music, **doesn't she?** · They **went** home, **didn't they?**
- Negative sentence → positive tag: He **can't** swim, **can he?** · You **haven't** finished, **have you?**

Special cases: I am late, **aren't I?** · Let's go, **shall we?**

School vocabulary: **timetable**, **subject**, **to pass / to fail an exam**, **mark** (the score you get), **headmaster**, **classmate**, **to skip a class**.

Practice: 1. Kofi is your brother, ___? 2. You don't like maths, ___? 3. They have finished, ___?
prog-2nde-1.title: Tenses review and question tags

prog-cp1-1.body:
Say hello in English: **Hello!** · **Good morning!** · **Goodbye!** · **Bye-bye!**

Your name: **What's your name?** → **My name is** Esi.

Colours: **red** · **blue** · **yellow** · **green** · **black** · **white**.

The flag of Togo is **green**, **yellow**, **red** and **white**!

Game: show an object in the classroom and say its colour: **It's red!**
prog-cp1-1.title: Hello and colours

prog-1re-1.body:
**Second conditional** (imaginary situation in the present): **If** + past simple, **would** + verb. **If** I **had** money, I **would** build a school in my village. **If** I **were** you, I **would** study harder.

**Third conditional** (regret about the past): **If** + past perfect, **would have** + past participle. **If** he **had worked** harder, he **would have passed** the exam.

**I wish / If only**:
- wish about the present → past simple: I **wish** I **spoke** Chinese. **If only** I **were** taller!
- regret about the past → past perfect: I **wish** I **had listened** to my teacher.

Summary: type 1 = possible · type 2 = imaginary · type 3 = too late.

Practice: 1. If I (be) president, I (create) jobs for young people. 2. If she (leave) earlier, she (not / miss) the bus. 3. I wish I (have) a computer.
prog-1re-1.grammar: second and third conditionals · I wish / If only
prog-1re-1.title: Wishes and regrets

prog-2nde-3.body:
After some verbs, we use the **gerund** (**-ing**); after others, the **infinitive** (**to** + verb).

Verbs + **-ing**: **enjoy**, **like / love / hate**, **finish**, **avoid**, **mind**, **keep**, **be good at**, **be interested in**, **look forward to**. I **enjoy reading**. She is **good at dancing**. I **look forward to meeting** you.

Verbs + **to**: **want**, **decide**, **hope**, **plan**, **learn**, **refuse**, **promise**, **would like**. I **want to become** an engineer. We **decided to play** basketball.

After a preposition, always **-ing**: Thank you **for helping** me.

Change of meaning: **stop smoking** (no longer smoke) ≠ **stop to smoke** (stop what you are doing in order to smoke). **remember to lock** (do not forget to lock) ≠ **remember locking** (have a memory of locking).

Practice: 1. I enjoy (listen) to music. 2. She wants (visit) Accra. 3. He is interested in (learn) Chinese.
prog-2nde-3.title: Hobbies and free time

prog-universite-4.body:
A **CV** (British English) or **résumé** (American English) is **1 to 2 pages** long.

Sections: **Personal details** · **Profile** (2–3 lines) · **Education** · **Work experience** · **Skills** (languages, computer skills) · **Interests** · **References**.
List your experience and education from the most **recent** to the oldest. Use **action verbs**: **managed**, **organised**, **designed**, **improved**, **led**.

The **cover letter** (a letter that explains why you want the job):
1. **Why you are writing**: I am writing to apply for the position of…
2. **Why you**: My degree in… and my experience in… have prepared me to…
3. **Why them**: I am particularly interested in your company because…
4. **Closing**: I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my application.

Avoid mistakes: ask someone to check your CV, and adapt it to each job offer.
prog-universite-4.title: Writing a CV and a cover letter

prog-4e-1.body:
The **past simple** tells about a finished action in the past: **yesterday**, **last week**, **last year**, **two days ago**, **in 2020**.

Regular verbs: add **-ed**: visit → visit**ed**, play → play**ed**, study → stud**ied**, stop → sto**pped**.

Irregular verbs to learn by heart: go → **went**, see → **saw**, eat → **ate**, have → **had**, buy → **bought**, come → **came**, take → **took**, make → **made**, get → **got**, swim → **swam**.

Negative: **didn't** + base verb: I **didn't go** to Kara. Question: **Did** you **visit** Kpalimé? → **Yes, I did.** / **No, I didn't.**

To be: I / he / she **was** · you / we / they **were**.

Example: Last holidays, I **went** to Aného with my cousins. We **swam** in the sea and **ate** fresh fish. It **was** wonderful!

Practice: 1. We (visit) our grandparents last month. 2. She (not / buy) a dress. 3. ___ you (see) the match yesterday?
prog-4e-1.title: My last holidays

prog-cm2-4.body:
To stay healthy:

**Wash your hands** with soap. · **Brush your teeth** every morning. · **Drink clean water.** · **Sleep under a mosquito net.** · **Eat fruits and vegetables.**

Advice with **should**: **You should** sleep early. · **You shouldn't** eat too many sweets.

When you are ill: **I'm sick.** · **I have a headache.** (my head hurts) · **Go to the hospital.**
prog-cm2-4.title: Healthy habits

prog-4e-4.body:
**must**: strong obligation. You **must** wash your hands before eating. **mustn't**: it is not allowed. You **mustn't** drink dirty water.

**should**: advice. You **should** sleep under a mosquito net. You **shouldn't** eat too much sugar.

**can**: ability or permission. I **can** swim. **Can** I go out, please? **can't**: I **can't** come today.

After a modal: base verb, no -s, no to: She **must go** (not she musts go / must to go).

Health: **malaria**, **fever** (a high body temperature), **headache** (pain in the head), **cough**, **stomachache**, **to be ill / sick**, **medicine**, **nurse**, **hospital**.

Giving advice: What's the matter? → I've got a headache. → You **should** take some rest and drink water.

Practice: 1. You ___ wear a helmet on a motorbike (obligation). 2. You ___ see a doctor (advice). 3. ___ you help me, please?
prog-4e-4.title: Health and good habits

prog-adultes-3.body:
**Common questions** and ways to answer:

- **Tell me about yourself.** → **I'm a dynamic and organised person. I have a degree in management and I have worked in sales for four years.**
- **Why do you want this job?** → **I'm interested in this position because**…
- **What are your strengths?** → **I'm reliable, I learn quickly and I work well in a team.**
- **What is your main weakness?** → **I sometimes spend too much time on details, but I'm learning to manage my time better.**
- **Where do you see yourself in five years?** → **I hope to have more responsibilities in the company.**

To talk about your experience, use the **present perfect** (experience up to today): **I have managed** a team of five people. Use the **past simple** for a job that is finished: **In 2021, I worked** for an NGO.

**Ending**: **Do you have any questions for us?** → **Yes, what does a typical day look like?** · **Thank you for your time.**

Practice: prepare your answer to "Tell me about yourself" in 5 sentences.
prog-adultes-3.title: The job interview

prog-cm1-4.body:
Prepositions of place: **in** · **on** · **under** · **next to** · **behind** · **in front of**.

**The book is on the table.** · **The cat is under the chair.** · **My bag is next to the door.**

Question: **Where is my pen?** → **It's in your bag!**
prog-cm1-4.title: Where is it?

prog-5e-4.body:
The **present continuous** is for an action **happening right now**.

Form: **to be** + verb + **-ing**. I **am reading**. She **is cooking**. They **are playing** football.

Negative: I **am not** sleeping. He **isn't** working. Question: **Are you** listening? **What is she doing?**

Spelling: write → writ**ing** (remove the e) · swim → swi**mming** (double the consonant) · play → play**ing**.

Signal words: **now**, **right now**, **at the moment**, **Look!**, **Listen!**

Present simple or present continuous? I **go** to school every day (habit). Today I **am staying** at home (right now).

Practice: 1. Look! The children (run). 2. My mother (cook) now. 3. What (you / do)?
prog-5e-4.title: What are you doing now?

prog-2nde-8.body:
A formal letter (asking for an internship, applying for a job, making a complaint) follows clear rules.

Top right: **your address** and the **date** (12th October 2026). On the left: the **name and address** of the person you are writing to.

Greeting: **Dear Sir or Madam,** (name unknown) · **Dear Mr Agbeko,** / **Dear Mrs Lawson,** (name known).

Introduction: **I am writing to apply for**… · **I am writing to ask for information about**… · **I am writing to complain about**…

Body: polite style, no contractions (**I am**, not I'm). **I would be grateful if you could**… · **Please find enclosed my CV.**

Conclusion: **I look forward to hearing from you.**

Closing: **Yours faithfully,** (after Dear Sir or Madam) · **Yours sincerely,** (when you know the name) + signature and full name.
prog-2nde-8.title: Writing a formal letter

prog-ce2-2.body:
The 7 days: **Monday** · **Tuesday** · **Wednesday** · **Thursday** · **Friday** · **Saturday** · **Sunday**.

**What day is it today?** → **Today is Monday.**

On Saturdays I go to the market: **On Saturday, I go to the market.**

On Sundays I rest: **On Sunday, I rest.**

Tip: in English, days always start with a **capital letter**.
prog-ce2-2.title: The days of the week

prog-tle-3.body:
**used to** + verb: a past habit that does not exist any more. I **used to** walk to school, but now I take a taxi-moto. Question: **Did** you **use to** play football?

**be used to** + **-ing**: be familiar with something. I **am used to getting** up early. **get used to** + **-ing**: become familiar with something. She is **getting used to living** in Lomé.

**Causative form** (someone else does something for you):
- **have** + object + past participle: I **had my phone repaired**. (A repairer fixed it for me.)
- **get** + object + past participle (more common): We **got the house painted**.
- **have** + person + base verb: I **had the mechanic check** the brakes.
- **get** + person + **to** + verb: She **got her brother to help** her.

**would rather** + base verb: prefer. I **would rather stay** at home.
**had better** + base verb: it is a good idea to. You **had better revise** tonight.

Practice: 1. When I was a child, I (used to / be used to) climb mango trees. 2. I got my hair (cut) yesterday. 3. You'd better (not / be) late.
prog-tle-3.grammar: used to / be used to · causative have / get
prog-tle-3.title: Advanced grammar for the BAC

prog-adultes-1.body:
**Introducing yourself**: **Hello, my name is** Kossi Amegah. **I work as** an accountant **at** a bank in Lomé. · **I'm in charge of** customer service. · **I've been working here for** five years.

**Introducing someone**: **Let me introduce** my colleague, Mrs Adjo. · **This is** Mr Lawson, **our new manager**.

Answering: **Nice to meet you.** → **Nice to meet you too.** · **Pleased to meet you.**

**Small talk** (light, friendly conversation): **How was your trip?** · **Is this your first time in Lomé?** · **What do you do?** · **Have you been working here long?**

Jobs: **accountant**, **engineer**, **nurse**, **teacher**, **driver**, **sales representative**, **shop owner**, **civil servant** (a person who works for the government), **entrepreneur**.

Practice: write 4 sentences to introduce yourself to an English-speaking client.
prog-adultes-1.title: Introducing yourself at work

prog-3e-3.body:
The **first conditional** expresses a real condition and its probable result.

Form: **If** + present simple, **will** + verb. **If** we **cut** all the trees, the desert **will** advance. **If** you **throw** plastic bags in the street, the gutters **will** be blocked.

You can change the order: The town **will** be cleaner **if** everybody **helps**. Be careful: never **will** after **if**.

**unless** = if… not: You will be ill **unless** you drink clean water.

Vocabulary: **pollution**, **waste** (rubbish), **plastic bags**, **deforestation**, **to plant trees**, **to recycle**, **to protect**, **flood** (too much water covering the land), **drought** (a long time with no rain), **climate change**.

Practice: 1. If it (rain), the road (be) flooded. 2. If we (plant) trees, we (have) more shade. 3. You will fail ___ you work hard (unless / if).
prog-3e-3.title: Protecting our environment

prog-cp1-3.body:
Shapes: **a circle** · **a square** · **a triangle** · **a rectangle** · **a star** · **a heart**.

Size: **big** · **small** · **long** · **short**.

**It's a big circle.** · **It's a small star.**

Question: **What shape is it?** → **It's a triangle.**

Game: draw a shape, and your neighbour says its name in English.
prog-cp1-3.title: Shapes and sizes

prog-5e-8.body:
Appearance: **tall** · **short** · **slim** (thin) · **fat** · **young** · **old** · **beautiful** · **handsome** (good-looking, for a man).
Hair: **short hair**, **long hair**, **curly hair**, **braids**.

Character: **kind** (nice to others) · **funny** (makes you laugh) · **clever** (intelligent) · **shy** (quiet with new people) · **hard-working** (works a lot) · **lazy** (does not like to work).

Sentences: **She is tall and slim. She has got long braids.** · **My best friend is funny and kind.**

Questions: **What does he look like?** (asks about appearance) → **He's tall with short hair.** · **What is she like?** (asks about character) → **She's very kind.**
prog-5e-8.title: Describing people

prog-2nde-5.body:
The **past perfect** is for an action that happened **before** another past action.
Form: **had** + past participle. When I arrived, the film **had** already **started**.

Compare: When I arrived, the film **started** (it started at the moment I arrived) ≠ When I arrived, the film **had started** (it started before I arrived).

Common words: **already**, **just**, **before**, **after**, **by the time**, **never… before**.
**By the time** the police came, the thieves **had escaped**. · I **had never seen** the sea **before** I went to Lomé.

Negative: She **hadn't finished**. Question: **Had** you **eaten** before the match?
prog-2nde-5.title: Telling a story: the past perfect

prog-6e-9.body:
Parts of the body: **head, eyes, ears, nose, mouth, arms, hands, legs, feet**.

To give advice or an order, we use the **imperative** (the verb alone, with no subject):
- **Wash** your hands with soap.
- **Brush** your teeth twice a day.
- **Take** a shower every day.

To say "no": **Don't** + verb → **Don't touch** dirty water.
To make a suggestion: **Let's** + verb → **Let's wash** our hands!

Activity: write 4 hygiene rules for your class (2 with *Don't*).
prog-6e-9.title: My body and hygiene

prog-6e-10.body:
At the market, we ask the price with **How much is…?** (one thing) or **How much are…?** (several things).

- **How much is** this bag? — It's **2,000 francs**.
- **How much are** these tomatoes? — They're **500 francs**.

To buy: **I'd like** two kilos of rice, **please**. (= I want…, politely)
The seller says: **Anything else?** (Do you want something more?) — The customer: **That's all, thank you.**

Numbers: 10 **ten** · 20 **twenty** · 50 **fifty** · 100 **one hundred** · 1,000 **one thousand**.

Activity: act out the market scene with a classmate.
prog-6e-10.title: Shopping: How much is it?

prog-6e-11.body:
In the street, there is: **a road, a pavement, a zebra crossing, traffic lights, a bus, a motorbike, a bicycle**.

Traffic lights: **red** = stop · **orange** = wait · **green** = go.

Safety advice (imperative):
- **Look** left and right before you cross the road.
- **Use** the zebra crossing.
- **Stop** at the red light.
- **Don't run** across the road.
- **Wear** a helmet on a motorbike.

Prepositions: **on** the pavement · **at** the traffic lights · **across** the road · **near** the school.
prog-6e-11.title: Road safety

prog-6e-12.body:
Possessive adjectives go **before the noun** and agree with the **owner**:
**my** (I) · **your** (you) · **his** (he, a boy) · **her** (she, a girl) · **our** (we) · **their** (they).

- Kofi has a bike. **His** bike is blue.
- Ama has a book. **Her** book is red.

The **'s** shows who something belongs to:
- **Ama's** pen = the pen of Ama
- the **teacher's** desk = the desk of the teacher
- **my brother's** school

With a plural ending in -s: **the students'** books (apostrophe only).
prog-6e-12.title: My things: possessives and 's

prog-6e-13.body:
To ask simple questions:
- **How old** are you? — I'm **twelve**. (age)
- **How many** brothers do you have? — I have **two**. (number, with a plural noun)
- **Where** do you live? — I live **in Lomé**. (place)
- **What** is your name? — **My name is** Kossi.

The verb **be**: I **am** · you **are** · he/she/it **is** · we/you/they **are**.
Question: **Are** you a student? — Yes, I **am**. / No, I'm **not**.

Be careful: we say **I'm twelve** (not "I have twelve").
prog-6e-13.title: Asking questions: How old, How many, Where

prog-5e-9.body:
In a **village**: **farms, fields, a well, a market, a primary school**. In a **town or city**: **buildings, traffic, a hospital, a bank, shops, a stadium**.

We describe with **There is** (one thing) and **There are** (several things):
- **There is** a big market in my village.
- **There are** many cars in the city.
- **There isn't** a cinema here. · **There aren't** any banks.

Useful adjectives: **quiet** (calm, not noisy) · **noisy** (with a lot of sound) · **crowded** (full of people) · **clean** · **dirty** · **safe** (not dangerous).

Activity: describe your neighbourhood in 5 sentences (*There is… / There are…*).
prog-5e-9.title: Village life and town life

prog-5e-10.body:
In Togo, there are many ceremonies: **a wedding** (when two people get married), **a naming ceremony** (when a baby gets its name), **a funeral** (a ceremony after someone dies), **a festival** (a traditional celebration). Examples: the **Epe-Ekpe** festival in Aného or **Evala** in Kara.

To tell about a past ceremony, we use the **past simple**:
- Last Saturday, we **went** to a wedding. (go → went)
- People **danced**, **sang** and **ate** together.
- The bride **wore** a beautiful *pagne*. (wear → wore)

Useful words: **guests** (people who are invited) · **drums** · **costume** · **elders** (old, respected people) · **to celebrate**.

Activity: tell about a celebration in your village in 5 sentences in the past.
prog-5e-10.title: Traditional ceremonies in Togo

prog-5e-11.body:
At the hospital: **a doctor, a nurse, a patient, a pharmacy, medicine, an injection**.

Symptoms: **I have a headache / a stomach ache / a fever / a cough.**
To say where it hurts: **My head hurts.**

To give advice: **should** (it is a good idea) / **shouldn't** (it is not a good idea) + verb:
- You **should** go to the hospital.
- You **should** drink a lot of water and rest.
- You **shouldn't** take medicine without a doctor.

Preventing malaria: **sleep under a mosquito net**.
prog-5e-11.title: Health and the hospital

prog-5e-12.body:
Places: **a bus station, a train station, an airport, a taxi stand, a ticket office**. Documents: **a ticket, a passport, a boarding pass**.

At the station or the airport:
- **One ticket to Kara, please.**
- **What time does the bus leave?** — It leaves **at 8 a.m.**
- **Where is the check-in desk?**
- **Your flight is delayed.** (it will leave later)

Prepositions: **go to** Kara · **arrive in** a city / **at** the airport · **leave for** Accra · **travel by** bus / train / plane.
prog-5e-12.title: Travelling: station and airport

prog-5e-13.body:
**be going to** + verb → a **plan** or an intention you have already decided:
- I **am going to** visit my grandmother this weekend.
- They **are going to** build a new school.

**will** + verb → a **decision** at the moment of speaking, a **prediction**, a **promise**:
- It's hot. I **will** open the window.
- Tomorrow **will** be sunny.
- I **will** help you, I promise.

Negative: **I'm not going to** / **I won't** (= will not).
Questions: **Are** you **going to** study? · **Will** it rain?
prog-5e-13.title: The future: be going to and will

prog-5e-14.body:
We use **for** + a **period of time** and **since** + a **starting point** (a date, a time).

- I have lived in Lomé **for** ten years. (period: 10 years)
- I have lived in Lomé **since** 2016. (starting point: 2016)
- She has studied English **for** two hours.
- She has studied English **since** 8 o'clock.

Periods with **for**: a week · three days · a long time.
Starting points with **since**: Monday · January · 2020 · I was a child.

We use these words with **have/has + past participle** (present perfect).
prog-5e-14.title: For and since

prog-5e-15.body:
**Short adjectives**: **-er** (comparative) and **the -est** (superlative).
- tall → **taller than** → **the tallest**
- big → **bigger** → **the biggest** (double the last consonant)

**Long adjectives**: **more … than** and **the most …**
- beautiful → **more beautiful than** → **the most beautiful**

**Irregular**: good → **better** → **the best** · bad → **worse** → **the worst**.

- Kara is **bigger than** Atakpamé.
- Lomé is **the largest** city in Togo.

Equality: **as … as** → Ama is **as tall as** Kofi.
prog-5e-15.title: Comparatives and superlatives

prog-4e-9.body:
**Countable** foods can be counted: **an egg, two tomatoes, three onions**. **Uncountable** foods cannot: **rice, water, oil, salt, flour**.

For quantity: **a kilo of** rice · **a litre of** oil · **a spoon of** sugar · **a piece of** meat.

Recipe verbs: **wash, peel** (take off the skin), **cut, boil** (cook in very hot water), **fry** (cook in hot oil), **mix** (put things together), **add** (put in more), **serve**.

A simple recipe: **First**, wash the rice. **Then**, boil water. **Next**, add the rice and salt. **Finally**, serve it hot.

Sequence words: **first → then → next → finally**.
prog-4e-9.title: Food and cooking

prog-4e-10.body:
Problems: **pollution, deforestation** (cutting down forests), **waste** (rubbish), **drought** (a long time with no rain), **floods** (too much water on the land). Solutions: **plant trees, recycle, save water, sort waste**.

To talk about obligation and advice:
- We **must** protect nature. (strong obligation)
- We **should** plant more trees. (advice)
- We **mustn't** throw rubbish in the river. (not allowed)

Cause and result: **because** (gives the reason) and **so** (gives the result):
- There is a lot of waste, **so** the river is dirty.
- The river is dirty **because** people throw rubbish in it.
prog-4e-10.title: Environment and nature

prog-4e-11.body:
Jobs: **a farmer, a teacher, a doctor, a driver, a tailor, a mechanic, an engineer, a lawyer, a journalist**.

To ask about a job: **What does your father do?** — **He is a driver.** / **He works in a hospital.**

We say **He is a** + job (with **a / an**):
- She is **a** nurse. · He is **an** engineer. (vowel → an)
