Present simple, 3rd person: add **-s** → He **works**, she **teaches**, he **fixes** cars.
The verb **have** → **has**, **go** → **goes**, **study** → **studies**.

Activity: “What do you want to be?” → **I want to be** a doctor **because** I like helping people.
prog-4e-11.grammar: What does he do? · present simple
prog-4e-11.title: Jobs and professions

prog-4e-12.body:
Vocabulary: **a phone, a computer, a keyboard, a screen, a mouse, the internet, a message, an app, a password, a charger**.

What you can do: **I can** send a message · **I can** search the internet · **I can** take a photo · **I can't** open this file.

Instructions: **Turn on** the computer. **Click** the icon. **Type** your name. **Save** the file. **Turn off** the phone.

Safety: **Never share your password.** **Don't open** strange links.

To ask for help: **Can you help me, please?** — **Sure!**
prog-4e-12.title: Technology: phones and computers

prog-4e-13.body:
The **present perfect** = **have / has + past participle**. We use it for:
1. an **experience**: I **have visited** Accra.
2. a **recent** action with a result now: She **has lost** her phone.
3. an action that **continues** until now (with for / since).

Questions: **Have** you **ever** eaten *fufu*? — Yes, I **have**. / No, I **haven't**.
Words: **ever** (at any time, in questions) · **never** (not at any time) · **just** (a very short time ago) · **already** · **yet**.

Irregular participles: go → **gone** · see → **seen** · eat → **eaten** · do → **done** · write → **written**.
prog-4e-13.title: Present perfect

prog-4e-14.body:
Modal verbs are followed by the **verb without to** and never take -s.

- **can**: ability / permission → I **can** swim. **Can** I come in?
- **must**: strong obligation → You **must** wear a uniform.
- **mustn't**: not allowed → You **mustn't** use your phone in class.
- **should**: advice → You **should** revise every day.
- **have to**: obligation (a rule from outside) → I **have to** wake up at 5.

Be careful: **don't have to** = it is not necessary (≠ mustn't).
prog-4e-14.title: Can, must and should

prog-4e-15.body:
We point to things with a **demonstrative**:

| | near | far |
|---|---|---|
| singular | **this** | **that** |
| plural | **these** | **those** |

- **This** book is mine. (here, one book)
- **That** house is big. (over there)
- **These** pens are new. (here, many)
- **Those** students are my friends. (over there, many)

Without a noun: **What is this?** — **It's** a calculator. · **What are those?** — **They're** goats.
prog-4e-15.title: This, that, these, those

prog-3e-9.body:
**Children's rights**: **the right to education, to health care, to a name and a nationality, to play, to be protected from violence**.

- Every child **has the right to** go to school.
- Children **should** be protected from **child labour** (children doing hard work for money).
- Parents **must** send their children to school.

To talk about rights: **right** (what you can have or do) · **duty** (what you must do) · **protect** · **equal** · **respect**.

**Universal Children's Day**: we celebrate children's rights on **20 November**.

Activity: write 3 rights and 3 duties of a student.
prog-3e-9.grammar: have the right to · must · should
prog-3e-9.title: Children's rights

prog-3e-10.body:
A **citizen** (a member of a country) has **rights** and **duties**:
- **vote** in elections (when you are 18)
- **pay taxes** · **obey the law** · **respect** others · **protect** public property
- **keep** the school and the streets **clean**

Useful sentences:
- A good citizen **must** respect the law.
- We **should** help our neighbours.
- Citizens **have to** pay taxes.

Words: **community** (the people who live in one place) · **government** · **law** · **election** · **volunteer** (a person who works for free to help).
prog-3e-10.title: Citizenship

prog-3e-11.body:
The **media**: **television, radio, newspapers, the internet, social networks**. A **journalist** writes or presents the **news** (new information about events).

Advantages / dangers:
- **Radio** is cheap and reaches villages.
- **Social media** helps us **communicate** quickly, **but** there is a lot of **fake news** (false information).

Advice: **Check** the source. **Don't share** a message you don't trust. **Think before you post.**

To give your opinion: **In my opinion…** · **I think that…** · **I agree / disagree.**
prog-3e-11.title: Media and communication

prog-3e-12.body:
In **group work**, we make suggestions and agree together:
- **Let's** start with the introduction.
- **Why don't we** share the tasks?
- **Shall we** meet at 3 p.m.?

Answers: **Good idea!** · **I agree.** · **I'm not sure. What about…?**

Roles: **the leader** (guides the group) · **the secretary** (writes) · **the speaker** (presents).
Good habits: **listen** to others · **share** ideas · **respect** each person · **finish** on time.
prog-3e-12.grammar: let's · why don't we · shall we
prog-3e-12.title: Working in a group

prog-3e-13.body:
The **first conditional** talks about a **possible situation in the future**:

**If + present simple, will + verb**
- **If** it **rains**, we **will stay** at home.
- **If** you **study**, you **will pass** the exam.
- **If** I **have** time, I **will call** you.

Negative: **If you don't hurry, you won't catch the bus.**
Other order (no comma): **We will stay at home if it rains.**

Be careful: after **if**, never **will** → ✗ If it *will rain*… ✓ If it **rains**…
prog-3e-13.title: Conditional type 1

prog-3e-14.body:
The **second conditional** talks about an **imaginary or unlikely** situation (now or in the future):

**If + past simple, would + verb**
- **If** I **were** president, I **would build** more schools.
- **If** I **had** a car, I **would drive** to Kara.
- **If** she **knew** the answer, she **would tell** us.

For **be**, use **were** with all persons: *If I were you, I would study.*

**If I were you, I would…** = a way to give advice.
Negative: **I wouldn't** (would not).
prog-3e-14.title: Conditional type 2

prog-3e-15.body:
In the **passive voice**, the object of the action becomes the subject: **be + past participle** (+ **by** + who does it).

- Active: Farmers **grow** cocoa. → Passive: Cocoa **is grown** by farmers.
- Active: The pupils **wrote** the letters. → Passive: The letters **were written** by the pupils.
- Future: The school **will be built** next year.

We use the passive when **the action** is more important than **who** does it:
- English **is spoken** in many countries.
- The bridge **was built** in 2010.

Question: **Where is** cotton **grown** in Togo?
prog-3e-15.title: The passive voice

prog-3e-16.body:
**BEPC written exam**: reading a text, vocabulary/grammar, translation and writing.

**1. Reading**: read the text **twice**. Read the questions. Answer in **your own words** when you can. For “True or False”, **justify** with a sentence from the text.

**2. Grammar**: find the **tense** (clue words: *yesterday*, *since*, *tomorrow*, *if*).

**3. Translation**: translate the **meaning**, not word for word.

**4. Writing (80 words)**: **Introduction** → **ideas + examples** → **conclusion**. Check: capital letters, tenses, agreement.

**5. Oral**: speak slowly, look at the person you are talking to, use simple and correct sentences.
prog-3e-16.title: BEPC practice: reading, writing and speaking

prog-2nde-9.body:
The big **public health** challenges in Togo: **malaria**, **HIV/AIDS**, **cholera**, **malnutrition** (not enough good food).

**Malaria**: carried by the **mosquito** (the female Anopheles). Prevention: **sleep under a mosquito net**, **clear stagnant water**, **seek treatment early**.
**HIV/AIDS**: passed on through **blood**, unprotected sex and from mother to child. Prevention: **use protection**, **get tested**, **never share needles**. An HIV-positive person can **live a long, healthy life** with treatment.
**Hygiene**: **wash your hands with soap**, **drink clean water**, **keep latrines clean**.

Structures: **can be prevented** (we can stop it before it happens) · **is caused by** (comes from) · **It is important to…**
prog-2nde-9.title: Public health: malaria, HIV/AIDS and hygiene

prog-2nde-10.body:
**New technologies**: **smartphones, the internet, social networks, e-learning, mobile money**.

**Advantages**: we can **communicate** quickly, **learn** online, **pay** by mobile money, **find** information.
**Disadvantages**: **addiction**, **fake news**, **cyberbullying**, **less face-to-face contact**.

To organise an opinion:
- **On the one hand,** technology saves time. **On the other hand,** it can be addictive.
- **Thanks to** the internet, students can learn anywhere.
- **Because of** social media, some young people sleep less.

**thanks to** = because of something good · **because of** = often because of something bad.
prog-2nde-10.title: New technologies

prog-2nde-11.body:
**Youth** (young people) and **education**: **primary, secondary, university, vocational training** (learning a job or a trade).

Talking about your plans:
- I **want to** become an engineer.
- I **would like to** study abroad.
- I **hope to** get a scholarship (**money to pay for your studies**).

Challenges for young people: **unemployment** (having no job), **lack of funds**, **early marriage**, **dropping out** (leaving school too early).

Solutions: **vocational training**, **entrepreneurship** (starting your own business), **free school meals**, **scholarships for girls**.

**Education is the key to development.**
prog-2nde-11.grammar: wish · want to · would like to
prog-2nde-11.title: Youth and education

prog-2nde-12.body:
**Past continuous** (**was/were + -ing**): an action **in progress** in the past.
- At 8 p.m., I **was studying**. · They **were playing** football when it started to rain.

**Past simple**: a **short** action that interrupts.
- I **was cooking** when the phone **rang**.

**Past perfect** (**had + past participle**): an action that happened **before** another past action.
- When I arrived, the lesson **had started**.
- She **had finished** her homework before she watched TV.

**Order**: 1) the older action → past perfect · 2) the more recent action → past simple.
prog-2nde-12.title: Past continuous and past perfect

prog-2nde-13.body:
**Linking words** connect ideas:

- **Addition**: **and**, **also**, **moreover**, **furthermore**
- **Contrast**: **but**, **however**, **although / even though**, **while**
- **Cause**: **because**, **since**, **because of**
- **Result**: **so**, **therefore**, **as a result**
- **Order**: **first**, **then**, **finally**

Examples:
- **Although** it was raining, we went out.
- He studied hard. **Therefore**, he passed.
- Technology is useful. **However**, it can be dangerous.

**However / therefore**: punctuation → **However,** (with a comma).
prog-2nde-13.title: Logical connectors

prog-2nde-14.body:
An **informal letter** (to a friend) follows this plan:

**1. Address + date** (top right): *Lomé, 12 October 2026*
**2. Greeting**: **Dear Ama,**
**3. Introduction**: **How are you? I hope you are fine.** · **Thank you for your letter.**
**4. Body**: your news, a question, one idea per paragraph.
**5. Conclusion**: **Write soon.** · **Give my regards to your family.** · **Say hello to…**
**6. Ending**: **Yours,** · **Best wishes,** · **Love,** + **your first name**.

Style: **contractions** (I'm, don't), simple expressions, a warm and friendly tone.
prog-2nde-14.title: Writing an informal letter

prog-1re-9.body:
The **Commonwealth of Nations** is a group of countries (many were British colonies) that work together: **education, trade, democracy, sport**. **Togo** joined the Commonwealth in **2022**.

Political systems: **a democracy** (the people vote) · **a monarchy** (a king or a queen) · **a republic** · **a dictatorship** (one person has all the power).

Vocabulary: **president, prime minister, parliament, government, election, vote, constitution, law, citizen**.

Sentences:
- In a democracy, leaders **are elected** by the people.
- The law **is made** by Parliament.
- The Commonwealth **promotes** democracy and human rights.
prog-1re-9.title: Governance and the Commonwealth

prog-1re-10.body:
**Gender equality** = **women** and **men** have the **same rights and opportunities**.

Challenges: **early marriage, unequal pay, violence against women, fewer girls in science**. **Stereotypes** (fixed ideas about roles): “girls cook, boys work”.

Solutions: **educate girls**, **equal pay**, **laws against violence**, **women in leadership**.

Opinion phrases: **In my view…** · **I strongly believe that…** · **It is unfair that…**
- Women **should have** the same opportunities as men.
- Many girls **are forced** to leave school.
- **Equal pay** means the same salary for the same work.
prog-1re-10.title: Gender equality

prog-1re-11.body:
Water is essential, but it is in danger because of **water pollution**.

**Causes**: **domestic waste**, **industrial waste**, **chemicals** from farms (pesticides), **plastic bags**, **oil spills**.
**Effects**: **diseases** (cholera, typhoid), **dead fish**, **less drinking water**.
**Solutions**: **treat waste water**, **ban plastic bags**, **plant trees along rivers**, **educate people**.

Structures:
- Rivers **are polluted by** factories. (passive)
- **As a result**, people fall ill.
- If we **don't act**, the water **will become** undrinkable.
prog-1re-11.title: Water pollution

prog-1re-12.body:
Togo has **national parks** like **Fazao-Malfakassa** and **Kéran**: they protect **wildlife** (wild animals) and **flora** (plants).

Threats: **poaching** (killing animals against the law), **illegal hunting**, **deforestation**, **bushfires**.
Protection: **laws**, **park rangers** (people who guard the park), **ecotourism**, **education**.

Opinions:
- Hunting **should be controlled** to protect animals.
- Poaching **must be stopped**.
- **Ecotourism** brings money **without destroying** nature.

Animals: **elephant, lion, antelope, monkey, crocodile, hippopotamus**.
prog-1re-12.title: National parks and hunting

prog-1re-13.body:
**Cybercrime** = crimes done on the internet: **hacking, online scams** (tricks to steal money), **identity theft, phishing, cyberbullying**.

**Victims** lose money, data and their reputation.

Protect yourself:
- **Use strong passwords** (letters, numbers, symbols).
- **Never click** on suspicious links.
- **Don't share** personal data.
- **Report** the problem to the police.

Present perfect for a recent situation: **Cybercrime has increased** in recent years.
Future: **If you share your password, someone will steal your account.**
prog-1re-13.title: Cybercrime and the internet

prog-1re-14.body:
**Patriotism** = **love for your country**: **respect the flag, the national anthem, the law**, and **serve** your community. In Togo: the flag, the national anthem and the motto **Travail – Liberté – Patrie** (Work – Freedom – Homeland).

**Cultural heritage** (the traditions and places we receive from the past): **traditional dances, music, masks, crafts, kente and pagne cloth, Koutammakou** (on the **UNESCO** World Heritage list).

**Tourism**: **a tourist** visits a place; tourism brings **jobs** and **money**.

Relative clauses:
- Koutammakou is a place **which** is protected by UNESCO.
- An artist is **someone who** creates art.
- The festival **that** I like most is Epe-Ekpe.
prog-1re-14.title: Patriotism, art and cultural heritage

prog-1re-15.body:
The **third conditional** talks about an **unreal situation in the past** (we cannot change it now):

**If + past perfect, would have + past participle**
- **If** I **had studied**, I **would have passed**. (but I did not study)
- **If** they **had left** earlier, they **wouldn't have missed** the bus.
- **If** she **had known**, she **would have helped**.

To express a **regret**: **I wish I had listened.** = I am sorry that I did not listen.

Be careful: never **would** in the **if** part.
prog-1re-15.grammar: if + past perfect, would have + p.p.
prog-1re-15.title: Conditional type 3

prog-1re-16.body:
A **speech** has 3 parts:

**1. Opening**: greet people and get their attention → **Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Today, I want to talk about…**
**2. Body**: 2 or 3 ideas, each with **an example** → **First… Second… Moreover…**
**3. Closing**: sum up and call people to action → **To conclude… Let us act now!**

Techniques to persuade:
- **Rhetorical question**: *Do we want a clean future?*
- **Repetition**: *We must act. We must act together.*
- **Rule of three**: *safe, clean and green.*
- **Inclusive words**: **we, us, our**.

Tone: **clear, confident, respectful**.
prog-1re-16.title: Writing a speech

prog-1re-17.body:
**Version**: translating from English into French. **Thème**: translating from French into English.

**Method**: 1) read the whole text · 2) find the **tenses** · 3) translate the **meaning**, not word for word · 4) read it again and check the **grammar**.

**False friends** (words that look the same but have a different meaning):
- **actually** = in fact (for “now”, say *currently*)
- **to attend** = to go to / be present at (for “wait”, say *to wait*)
- **library** = a place where you borrow books (a place where you buy books is a *bookshop*)
- **sensible** = reasonable, with good judgement (easily hurt or upset is *sensitive*)

**Word order**: the adjective comes **before** the noun → *a beautiful house*.
**In English**, a verb always has a subject → *It is raining.*
prog-1re-17.title: Translation: version and thème

prog-tle-9.body:
**Globalisation** = the **world-wide connection** of economies, cultures and communication.

**Advantages**: **free trade**, **cheaper products**, **cultural exchange**, **jobs**, **fast information** (internet).
**Disadvantages**: **loss of local cultures**, **unfair competition** for small farmers, **inequality**, **pollution** from transport.

Structures for arguing:
- **Admittedly**, globalisation creates jobs. **Nevertheless**, it increases inequality.
- **Not only** does it help trade, **but also** it spreads ideas. (inversion)
- **As a result of** globalisation, African products reach new markets.

Linking words: **nevertheless** (but still) · **whereas** (in contrast) · **consequently** (as a result).
prog-tle-9.title: Globalisation

prog-tle-10.body:
**Emigration** = leaving your country; **immigration** = arriving in another country. A **migrant**, a **refugee** (a person who runs away from war or danger), an **asylum seeker**.

**Push factors** (reasons to leave): **poverty, unemployment, conflict, climate change**.
**Pull factors** (things that attract people): **better jobs, security, education, family abroad**.

Consequences: **brain drain** (educated people leave the country), **remittances** (money sent home to the family), **cultural diversity**, **integration** issues.

Sentences:
- Many young people **emigrate** in search of **better opportunities**.
- Migrants **may face** discrimination. (possibility)
- The minister **said** that the borders **would be** controlled.
prog-tle-10.title: Emigration and immigration

prog-tle-11.body:
**Human rights** are the rights of **all human beings**. The **Universal Declaration of Human Rights** was adopted by the **UN** (United Nations) in **1948**.

Basic rights: **the right to life, freedom of speech, freedom of religion, equality before the law, education, a fair trial** (a just and honest court case).

Violations: **torture, slavery, discrimination, child labour, arbitrary arrest**.

Sentences:
- Everyone **has the right to** freedom of expression.
- No one **shall be tortured**. (formal)
- Human rights **must be respected** by all governments.
- NGOs **defend** victims and **denounce** abuses.
prog-tle-11.title: Human rights

prog-tle-12.body:
**Sustainable development** = meeting the needs of **today** without harming the needs of **future generations**.

The 3 pillars: **economic growth**, **social progress**, **environmental protection**.

Examples: **renewable energy** (solar, wind), **recycling**, **organic farming**, **reforestation**, **clean water for all**. The UN **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**: 17 goals for 2030.

Sentences:
- We **need to** reduce our carbon footprint.
- **If** we use more solar energy, we **will reduce** pollution.
- Unless we act, the planet **will suffer**. (**unless** = if not)
- **Future generations** deserve a healthy planet.
prog-tle-12.title: Sustainable development

prog-tle-13.body:
**Democracy** = power to the people: **free elections, freedom of the press, independent justice, political pluralism**.

**Peace** needs: **dialogue, tolerance, justice, respect of differences, fight against corruption**.

Threats: **conflict, corruption, ethnic hatred, vote rigging** (cheating in elections).

Phrases for a debate:
- **I would argue that** dialogue is better than violence.
- **We should have** invested more in education to prevent conflict.
- **I wish** leaders **would listen** to young people.
- **Peace is not just the absence of war; it is also justice.**

Words: **mediator** (a person who helps two sides agree) · **ceasefire** (an agreement to stop fighting) · **reconciliation**.
prog-tle-13.title: Peace and democracy

prog-tle-14.body:
The **language register** changes with the situation.

| Informal | Formal |
|---|---|
| Hi, guys! | Dear Sir or Madam, |
| I wanna go | I would like to go |
| Can you…? | Would you be so kind as to…? |
| Thanks a lot | I am most grateful |
| Sorry | I apologise for… |
| Bye | Yours faithfully / Yours sincerely |

**Formal**: no contractions (*do not*), precise vocabulary, full sentences.
**Informal**: contractions (*don't*), everyday expressions.
**Literary**: images, a rich style.

**Rule**: *Dear Sir or Madam* → **Yours faithfully**. *Dear Mr Mensah* → **Yours sincerely**.
prog-tle-14.title: Language registers

prog-tle-15.body:
To **debate**: present your ideas, answer others and conclude with **respect**.

Structure: **Claim** (what you say is true) → **Evidence** (proof, an example) → **Explanation** → **Counter-argument** (the other side's idea) → **Rebuttal** (showing why that idea is wrong).

Phrases:
- **I would like to argue that…**
- **The evidence suggests that…**
- **Some people claim that… However, …**
- **I partly agree, but…** · **I respectfully disagree because…**

Analysing a document: **Who wrote it? When? For whom? What is the main idea? What is the author's opinion? Is the evidence reliable?**

Words: **bias** (an unfair, one-sided view) · **source** · **reliable** (you can trust it) · **claim** · **statistics**.
prog-tle-15.title: Debating and critical analysis

prog-universite-7.body:
**Business English** (Management, Law, Economics): **a company, a client, a supplier, an invoice, a contract, a budget, profit, loss, a deadline, a meeting**.

Useful expressions:
- **I am writing to enquire about…** · **Please find attached…**
- **We would like to confirm** our order.
- **The deadline is** the end of the month.
- **Could you send me a quotation?** (a document that gives the price)
- **The profit rose by 10%.** · **Sales fell sharply.**

Figures: **increase / rise** · **decrease / fall** · **remain stable** · **peak** · **hit a low**.
prog-universite-7.title: Business English

prog-universite-8.body:
**Scientific writing** uses the **passive** and a neutral tone:
- The samples **were collected** in March. · The experiment **was repeated** three times.

**IMRaD** structure: **I**ntroduction · **M**ethods · **R**esults · **a**nd **D**iscussion.

**Medical English**: **a patient, a symptom, a diagnosis, a treatment, a dose, a prescription, a side effect**.
- The patient **complained of** chest pain. · The doctor **prescribed** antibiotics.
- **Take two tablets** three times a day, **after meals**.

Science words: **a hypothesis, a variable, a sample, data, a result, a conclusion**.
prog-universite-8.theme: English for Specific Purposes: science and medicine
prog-universite-8.title: Medical and scientific English

prog-universite-9.body:
**Technical English**: **a server, a network, a database, software, hardware, a bug, a firewall, a circuit, a sensor, a voltage**.

**Instructions** (imperative): **Install** the software. **Restart** the computer. **Check** the connection. **Back up** your files.

**Descriptions** (passive): The data **is stored** in a database. The system **is protected** by a firewall.

**Reporting a problem**: **The network is down.** · **I can't log in.** · **The application keeps crashing.** · **Could you reset my password?**

Be precise: give **numbers + units**: *230 volts, 50 Hz, 8 GB of RAM*.
prog-universite-9.title: Technical English: IT and engineering

prog-universite-10.body:
**Phonetics** studies speech sounds; **phonology** studies how sounds are organised. We use the **IPA** (International Phonetic Alphabet).

Some difficult sounds for French speakers:
- **/θ/** (think) and **/ð/** (this): put your tongue between your teeth.
- **/h/**: breathe out (**house**); do not forget it.
- **/ɪ/** (ship) ≠ **/iː/** (sheep): short vowel / long vowel.
- **-ed**: /t/ (**worked**), /d/ (**played**), /ɪd/ (**wanted**).

**Word stress**: stress can change the meaning → **'record** (noun) vs **re'cord** (verb).
**Intonation**: rising for yes/no questions ↗, falling for open questions ↘.
prog-universite-10.title: Phonetics and phonology

prog-universite-11.body:
**Syntax** studies the structure of sentences; **semantics** studies their meaning.

Basic structure: **S**ubject + **V**erb + **O**bject → *Kofi (S) reads (V) a book (O).*
Parts: **noun phrase, verb phrase, adjective, adverb, clause** (a group of words with a subject and a verb).
- **Main clause**: *I stayed at home.* · **Subordinate clause**: *because it was raining.*

**Semantics**:
- **synonyms** (big / large) · **antonyms** (hot / cold) · **homonyms** (bank = a place for money / the side of a river)
- **denotation** (the literal meaning) vs **connotation** (the feelings or ideas linked to a word)

Example: *home* has a warm **connotation**; *house* is more neutral.

prog-universite-13.body:
The **United Kingdom** = **England, Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland**. Capital: **London**.

**Institutions**:
- **Monarchy** (constitutional): the king / queen **reigns but doesn't rule**.
- **Parliament**: **House of Commons** (elected) and **House of Lords**.
- **Prime Minister**: head of the government, from the majority party.

**History**: the **British Empire** (colonisation, including part of Africa), then **decolonisation** (1950s–60s) and the creation of the **Commonwealth**.

Words: **empire, colony, independence, constitution, devolution** (giving power to the regions).

**United States**: **50 states**, capital **Washington, D.C.** System: **federal republic**.

- **Executive**: the **President**
- **Legislative**: **Congress** = **Senate** + **House of Representatives**
- **Judicial**: the **Supreme Court**

prog-universite-15.body:
**Version** (EN → FR) and **thème** (FR → EN).

Translation techniques: **literal translation**, **transposition** (changing the word class), **modulation** (changing the point of view), **adaptation**, **borrowing** (using the foreign word).

Examples:
- *He swam across the river.* → in French, “swam” becomes a phrase meaning “by swimming” and “across” becomes the verb “crossed”. (transposition)
- *It's a 5-minute walk.* → becomes “it is 5 minutes on foot”. (modulation)
- **False friends**: *eventually* = in the end (for “maybe”, say *possibly*) · *injury* = a wound or hurt body part (a rude word is an *insult*) · *college* = a school for older students or a university.

Translating means first **understanding**, then **saying it again** naturally in the other language.
prog-universite-15.title: Translation: thème and version

prog-universite-16.body:
**Administrative writing**: official letters, reports, minutes, requests.

**Letter of application / request**:
**Sender's address → Date → Recipient → Subject line → Salutation → Body → Closing → Signature.**

**Subject**: **Re: Request for a scholarship.**
**Opening**: **I am writing to apply for / to request / to inform you that…**
**Closing**: **I look forward to hearing from you.** · **Yours faithfully / sincerely.**

**Report**: **Title, Introduction, Findings, Conclusion, Recommendations.**
Style: **objective, concise, polite, no contractions.**

prog-adultes-7.body:
A good **professional email** is short, clear and polite.

**Subject**: precise (*Meeting on Tuesday – confirmation*).
**Greeting**: **Dear Mr Mensah,** · **Dear Ms Ama Kossi,** · **Dear all,**
**Purpose**: **I am writing to…** · **I would like to…**
**Details**: date, time, documents.
**Closing**: **Thank you for your help.** · **Please let me know if you have any questions.**
**Sign-off**: **Kind regards,** · **Best regards,** + your name and job title.

Avoid: text-message abbreviations, capital letters everywhere (= shouting), very long sentences.
prog-adultes-7.title: Writing professional emails

prog-adultes-8.body:
Plan of a presentation: **Introduction → Main points → Conclusion → Questions.**

**Opening**: **Good morning, everyone. Thank you for coming. Today I'm going to talk about…**
**Plan**: **I will start with…, then I will move on to…, and finally…**
**Transitions**: **Let's move on to…** · **Turning to…** · **As you can see on this slide…**
**Closing**: **To sum up…** · **Thank you for listening. Are there any questions?**

Tips: **speak slowly**, **make eye contact**, **one idea per slide**, **use numbers and examples**.

Answering questions: **That's a good question.** · **Let me check and get back to you.**
prog-adultes-8.title: Giving a presentation

prog-adultes-9.body:
The **TOEIC** tests English **for work** (score out of **990**). Two sections:
- **Listening** (45 minutes, 100 questions): photos, question-response, conversations, short talks.
- **Reading** (75 minutes, 100 questions): incomplete sentences, text completion, reading comprehension.

**Strategies**:
1. Read the **questions before** you listen.
2. Don't get stuck: **go on** to the next one and come back later.
3. Answer **all** the questions (there is no penalty).
4. Learn work vocabulary: **invoice, schedule, deadline, branch, supplier, refund**.

**Traps**: words that look alike (*affect / effect*), prepositions (*by Friday / until Friday*).
prog-adultes-9.title: TOEIC preparation

prog-adultes-10.body:
**IELTS** (bands **1 to 9**) and **TOEFL iBT** (a test by ETS) are used to **study abroad**. Four skills: **Listening, Reading, Writing, Speaking**.

**Writing**: **Task 1** (describe a chart: *The chart shows…*) and **Task 2** (opinion essay, 250 words).
**Speaking**: **Part 1** (personal questions), **Part 2** (speak for 1–2 minutes on a topic), **Part 3** (discussion).

Phrases for a chart:
- **The number of students rose from 200 to 500.**
- **There was a sharp fall in 2020.**
- **It remained stable.**

Tip: practise with **past papers** and **time yourself**.
prog-adultes-10.title: IELTS and TOEFL preparation

prog-adultes-11.body:
The **CEFR** (Common European Framework of Reference) puts English into 6 levels:

| Level | Name | I can… |
|---|---|---|
| **A1** | Beginner | introduce myself, use very simple sentences |
| **A2** | Elementary | talk about my daily life |
| **B1** | Intermediate | manage when I travel, tell a story |
| **B2** | Upper-intermediate | discuss easily, write a clear text |
| **C1** | Advanced | speak fluently and with nuance |
| **C2** | Proficient | understand almost everything, sound very natural |

To improve: **listen daily**, **read short texts**, **speak every day**, **write a small diary**.

Goals: work → **B1/B2** · studying abroad → **B2/C1**.
